meaning_in_line: to moisten and nourish living things quietly
person_quality: quiet care that nourishes others without asking for notice or praise
line_original: 隨風潛入夜，潤物細無聲。
source: 杜甫「春夜喜雨」唐
sense_check: Confirms match: 潤 here means quietly nourishing living things without seeking notice, matching the gift-card sense of quiet, life-giving care.
context_check: positive — joyful poem celebrating timely spring rain bringing life to crops and the countryside
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 潤う/うるおい and ZH 滋潤/溫潤 carry warm, life-giving, prosperous associations; also attested in 『禮記・大學』「富潤屋，德潤身」and 『和漢朗詠集』菅原文時「花新開日初陽潤」)
notes: Theme: Care & nurture. Canonical 詩眼 (poetic eye) of Tang poetry; also appears in 『和漢朗詠集』巻上・雨「花の新たに開くる日初陽潤へり」.

meaning_in_line: to nurture and cultivate virtue through resolute action
person_quality: patient, steady cultivation that nurtures growth like a clear spring rising at the foot of a mountain
line_original: 蒙：山下出泉，蒙；君子以果行育德。
source: 『周易』大象・蒙卦（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 育 here means patiently cultivating and nurturing virtue through steady action, matching the gift-card sense of nurturing growth.
context_check: positive — the Hexagram Meng (Youthful Learning) likening education and personal growth to a pure mountain spring, inspiring the noble person to nurture virtue through decisive action (果行育德)
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 育てる/育む and ZH 培育/養育 are wholly positive; slightly institutional in compounds like 教育, but warm as 育む/育德)
notes: Theme: Care & nurture (Revised in v2: replaced cosmological 『中庸』「萬物育焉」 with the personal, human-focused 『周易・蒙卦』「君子以果行育德」).

meaning_in_line: to cherish, soothe, and care for each person with tender regard
person_quality: tender, attentive care that looks after everyone without leaving anyone behind
line_original: もののふの 八十伴男を 撫で賜ひ 整へ賜ひ 食す国の 四方の人をも あぶさはず 恵み賜へば
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第十九・4254 大伴家持（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 撫で賜ひ here means caring for and comforting people with tender, inclusive regard, matching the gift-card sense of affectionate care.
context_check: positive — celebratory choka by Otomo no Yakamochi praising benevolent care that cherishes every person ('撫で賜ひ 整へ賜ひ…あぶさはず 恵み賜へば', leaving no one out); in the original Man'yogana text (万葉集/第十九巻), 撫 is also written logographically as 「物乃布能 八十友之雄乎 撫賜 等登能倍賜」
standalone_reading_risk: JP: 撫でる (gentle stroking, positive); ZH: 撫養/安撫 (nurturing/soothing, positive). Minor caution: avoid pairing with 孤 (撫孤) in non-memorial contexts
notes: Theme: Care & nurture (Revised in v2: upgraded to a Man'yoshu line where 撫 appears directly in kanji in both the original Man'yogana text and Kamochi Masazumi's edition; also attested in 『万葉集』1・3「朝庭 取撫賜」).

meaning_in_line: to stroke a child's head gently while praying for their safe journey
person_quality: tender, hands-on parental affection whose blessing stays in the heart forever
line_original: 知々波々我 可之良加伎奈弖 佐久安例弖 伊比之氣等婆是 和須礼加祢豆流
source: 『万葉集』巻二十・4346 丈部稲麻呂（奈良時代・防人歌）
sense_check: Confirms match: 加伎奈弖 (かきなで) here means a parent gently stroking a child's head in blessing, matching the gift-card sense of tender parental care (written in man'yogana).
context_check: positive — deeply moving Sakimori poem remembering his parents stroking his head and saying 'Be safe and well' ('父母が頭掻き撫で幸くあれて言ひし言葉ぜ忘れかねつる')
standalone_reading_risk: none
notes: Theme: Care & nurture (Secondary reference row marked kana_only: yes, as 掻き撫で is written phonetically as 可之良加伎奈弖 in the original東歌/防人歌 orthography).

meaning_in_line: deeply loving, tender, and devoted
person_quality: unconditional maternal or parental love expressed through quiet, everyday acts
line_original: 慈母手中線，遊子身上衣。
source: 孟郊「遊子吟」唐
sense_check: Confirms match: 慈 here means a mother's deep, unconditional loving care stitched into her child's clothes, matching the gift-card sense of devoted love.
context_check: positive — universally beloved tribute to a mother stitching clothes before her child's journey, ending with gratitude ('誰言寸草心，報得三春暉')
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 慈しみ/慈愛 and ZH 慈愛/仁慈 are noble and warm; also grounded in 『老子』第67章「夫慈故能勇」and 『徒然草』第142段「恩愛の道ならでは、かゝるものゝ心に慈悲ありなむや」)
notes: Theme: Care & nurture. Best suited for parents, grandparents, and memorials.

meaning_in_line: to nourish and cultivate patiently as spring rain mothers the blossoms
person_quality: nurturing others as naturally and generously as spring rain brings flowers to life
line_original: 養得自為花父母。洗来寧弁薬君臣。
source: 『和漢朗詠集』巻上・春・雨 紀長谷雄「仙家春雨」（平安時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 養 here means nurturing and raising blossoms like a loving parent, matching the gift-card sense of patient, generous nurture.
context_check: positive — celebratory Heian kanshi in Wakan Roeishu praising spring rain that nourishes blossoms like a parent ('養ひ得ては自ら花の父母たり')
standalone_reading_risk: JP: 養う can imply financial support (扶養) or recuperation (養生) in prosaic usage; ZH: 涵養/培養 (positive). Pairing with this poetic line or 『孟子』「我善養吾浩然之氣」elevates it completely
notes: Theme: Care & nurture. Japanese Heian classic source (Kino Haseo in Wakan Roeishu); also attested in 『孟子・公孫丑上』「我善養吾浩然之氣」.

meaning_in_line: to shelter, protect, and sustain new life
person_quality: selfless devotion that continues to protect and nourish loved ones across seasons of life
line_original: 落紅不是無情物，化作春泥更護花。
source: 龔自珍「己亥雜詩（其五）」清
sense_check: Confirms match: 護 here means selflessly sheltering and sustaining new life, matching the gift-card sense of enduring protection.
context_check: positive — transforming departure from office into an affirming vow of ongoing devotion and nurturing of the next generation
standalone_reading_risk: JP: 護る (noble, protective, used for guarding sacred or precious things; note modern medical term 介護 in compounds); ZH: 守護/呵護 (warm and protective)
notes: Theme: Care & nurture. Especially resonant for retiring mentors, parents, and memorial gifts.

meaning_in_line: to prop up or physically support
person_quality: creating an upright, supportive presence that helps others stand tall naturally
line_original: 蓬生麻中，不扶而直。
source: 『荀子』勸學篇（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 扶 here means supporting and helping someone stand tall and straight, matching the gift-card sense of upright support.
context_check: positive — classic encouragement of learning and moral environment, showing how bent mugwort growing among straight hemp stands straight naturally
standalone_reading_risk: JP: 扶ける (literary/noble writing for 助ける; in compounds 扶養/扶助 can sound bureaucratic); ZH: 扶持/扶助 (positive, supportive)
notes: Theme: Care & nurture / Guidance. Praises a mentor,  family,  or team whose upright presence naturally uplifts others.

meaning_in_line: to scoop and cradle water in both cupped hands
person_quality: attentive, gentle presence that finds luminous beauty in small everyday moments
line_original: 掬水月在手，弄花香滿衣。
source: 于良史「春山夜月」唐
sense_check: Confirms match: 掬 here means gently cradling water in both hands so the moon rests in one's palms, matching the gift-card sense of attentive, tender care.
context_check: positive — serene, joyful spring night poem where every gesture in nature brings beauty and fragrance close
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 掬う/むすぶ and ZH 掬水/笑容可掬 are poetic, refined, and warm)
notes: Theme: Care & nurture. A textbook Tang 煉字: scooping water brings the moon itself into one's hands.

meaning_in_line: to wrap a thoughtful gift in white paper and attach it to a blooming plum branch
person_quality: thoughtful, tender care that wraps everyday gestures in beauty and warmth
line_original: 「頭辨 〈行成〉の御もとより」とてとのもづかさ、繪などやうなる物を白きしきしに包みて、梅の花のいみじく咲きたるにつけてもてきたる
source: 清少納言『枕草子』（國文大觀本）「頭辨の御もとより」（平安時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 包みて here means wrapping a thoughtful gift with beauty and care for someone dear, matching the gift-card sense of warm, considerate embrace.
context_check: positive — charming episode in The Pillow Book where Fujiwara no Yukinari sends a gift wrapped in white shikishi paper attached to a branch of beautifully blooming plum blossoms (also in 『枕草子』: Empress Teishi wrapping a single kerria petal「山吹の花びらを唯一つ包ませ給へり」)
standalone_reading_risk: none (JP 包む/包容力 and ZH 包容 are warm and embracing; also grounded in 『周易・泰卦』「包荒，得尚于中行，以光大也」for magnanimous inclusiveness)
notes: Theme: Care & nurture (Revised in v2: replaced Basho's pilgrimage head-cloth line with Sei Shonagon's plum-blossom gift-wrapping passage in Makura no Soshi + I Ching Hexagram Tai「包荒…以光大也」).

meaning_in_line: to hold, embrace, and make room for all people with gentle warmth
person_quality: spacious, unhurried generosity of heart that welcomes others just as they are
line_original: 唯天下至聖，為能聰明叡知，足以有臨也；寬裕溫柔，足以有容也；
source: 『禮記』中庸・第三十一章（先秦・秦漢）
sense_check: Confirms match: 容 here means embracing and making room for others with gentle, spacious warmth, matching the gift-card sense of generous acceptance.
context_check: positive — praising the supreme sage's combination of wisdom, gentle warmth, and all-embracing capacity (寬裕溫柔，足以有容也)
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 受け容れる/寛容 and ZH 包容/寬容 are deeply positive; also appears as a welcoming verb in 『おくのほそ道』「蜑のとまやに膝を容て雨のはるゝを待つ」)
notes: Theme: Care & nurture. Functions as a verbal nominalization ('having the capacity to embrace/hold') paired with 寬裕溫柔.

meaning_in_line: to bestow generous, all-embracing kindness without leaving anyone out
person_quality: warm, unstinting generosity of spirit that blesses and enriches everyone around them
line_original: もののふの 八十伴男を 撫で賜ひ 整へ賜ひ 食す国の 四方の人をも あぶさはず 恵み賜へば
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第十九・4254 大伴家持（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 恵み賜へば here means bestowing generous, inclusive kindness on all people, matching the gift-card sense of warm, unstinting grace.
context_check: positive — Otomo no Yakamochi's celebratory choka praising benevolent grace that reaches every person in all four directions without omission (あぶさはず 恵み賜へば); also in 『論語・陽貨』「恭、寬、信、敏、惠…惠則足以使人」
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 恵む/恵み and ZH 恩惠/賢惠/惠澤 are warm, auspicious, and generous)
notes: Theme: Care & nurture (Phase 2 Japanese classical expansion). 恵み賜へば appears directly in kanji in Kamochi Masazumi's Man'yoshu edition.

meaning_in_line: dear, cherished, and tenderly loved
person_quality: deep, unconditional affection that treasures family and loved ones above all else
line_original: 父母を 見れば貴し 妻子見れば めぐし愛し 世間は かくぞことわり
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第五・800 山上憶良（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 愛し here means cherishing family with deep, tender affection, matching the gift-card sense of unconditional love.
context_check: positive — Yamanoue no Okura's warm affirmation of family love ('めぐし愛し', read めぐしうつくし, 'dear and cherished'), echoed in his prose reflection in the same volume: 「至極の大聖すら、子を愛しむ心有り。況乎世間の蒼生、誰か子を愛まざる」and 『孟子・離婁下』「仁者愛人」
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 愛する/愛おしい and ZH 仁愛/摯愛 are universally positive; for non-romantic gifts such as parents or mentors, pairing with Okura's 『万葉集』or Mencius's「仁者愛人」frames 愛 as deep human affection and reverence)
notes: Theme: Care & nurture (Phase 2 Japanese classical expansion). 愛 appears directly in kanji in Kamochi Masazumi's Man'yoshu Vol. 5 (both poem 800 and Okura's prose essay).

meaning_in_line: to uphold and guard faithfulness and righteousness
person_quality: steadfast loyalty that quietly keeps promises and protects what matters most
line_original: 誠人能道をつとめ義を守べし名も又是にしたがふといへり
source: 松尾芭蕉『おくのほそ道』壺の碑・佐藤庄司旧跡（江戸時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 守べし here means steadfastly upholding faithfulness and duty, matching the gift-card sense of loyal protection and promise-keeping.
context_check: positive — deeply moved reflection praising the loyal wives and warriors of the Sato clan whose steadfast fidelity preserved their honor across centuries
standalone_reading_risk: JP: 守る (protective, loyal; minor sports/business idiom 守りに徹する 'playing it safe'); ZH: 守護/信守 (positive; 守舊 means conservative). Overall very safe and resonant
notes: Theme: Steadfast waiting & constancy (Live-test engine top choice). Also supported by 『老子』第16章「致虛極，守靜篤」.

meaning_in_line: to await the right moment with poised readiness
person_quality: patient, trusting readiness that waits without anxiety until the tide and moon are right
line_original: 熟田津尓 船乗世武登 月待者 潮毛可奈比沼 今者許藝乞菜
source: 『万葉集』巻一・8 額田王（飛鳥時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 待者 (待てば) here means waiting with calm, trusting readiness for the right tide and moon, matching the gift-card sense of patient waiting.
context_check: positive — triumphant, spirited departure poem ('熟田津に船乗りせむと月待てば潮もかなひぬ今は漕ぎ出でな'): waiting for the moon brings the rising tide, turning patience into collective momentum
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 待つ/期待 and ZH 等待/期待 are warm; avoids the melancholy of unrequited love poems by grounding in Nukata no Okimi's bright tide poem and Tao Yuanming's 『飲酒』「幽蘭生前庭，含薰待清風」)
notes: Theme: Steadfast waiting & constancy (Live-test engine top choice). 待 appears directly in kanji in the original Man'yoshu line (月待者).

meaning_in_line: enduring constancy and unwavering principle
person_quality: steady, unchanging reliability through every wind and thunderclap of life
line_original: 恆：雷風，恆；君子以立不易方。
source: 『周易』大象・恆卦（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 恆 (恒) here means standing firm with unchanging constancy through wind and thunder, matching the gift-card sense of enduring reliability.
context_check: positive — Great Commentary on the Hexagram Heng (Constancy), teaching how the noble person stands firm without losing direction amid thunder and wind
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 恒に/恒久 and ZH 恆心/永恆 express enduring constancy; also appears in exact Shinjitai/variant glyph 恒 in 『周易・家人卦』「君子以言有物，而行有恒」and 『孟子・離婁下』「愛人者，人恒愛之；敬人者，人恒敬之」)
notes: Theme: Steadfast waiting & constancy. Shinjitai 恒 / Kyujitai 恆; also attested verbatim as 恒 in 『孟子・離婁下』「愛人者，人恒愛之」.

meaning_in_line: everlasting, unchanged, and ever-fresh
person_quality: timeless, dependable presence that stays true and youthful in spirit across the years
line_original: 河上乃 湯津盤村二 草武左受 常丹毛冀名 常處女煮手
source: 『万葉集』巻一・22 吹芡刀自（飛鳥時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 常 here means remaining ever-fresh and unchanging across time, matching the gift-card sense of timeless dependability.
context_check: positive — auspicious celebratory poem composed at the sacred rock cluster by the river ('川の上のゆつ岩群に草生さず常にもがもな常処女にて'), wishing for eternal youth and constancy
standalone_reading_risk: JP: 常に/常しえ (poetic constancy) vs. 日常/尋常 ('ordinary/commonplace' in prosaic usage); ZH: 恆常 (constancy) vs. 平常 ('ordinary'). Best paired with『万葉集』or『周易・坎卦』「君子以常德行，習教事」
notes: Theme: Steadfast waiting & constancy (Live-test engine top choice). 常 appears twice in kanji in the original Man'yoshu text.

meaning_in_line: to be fully present and complete within oneself
person_quality: quiet preparedness and inner completeness that others can always lean on
line_original: 孟子曰：「萬物皆備於我矣，反身而誠，樂莫大焉。強恕而行，求仁莫近焉。」
source: 『孟子』盡心上（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 備 here means having sincere completeness and readiness within oneself, matching the gift-card sense of quiet preparedness others can rely on.
context_check: positive — uplifting philosophical declaration that all moral possibilities are already complete within us, bringing deep joy when we examine ourselves with sincerity (also 『荀子・勸學』「積善成德，而神明自得，聖心備焉」)
standalone_reading_risk: JP: 備える/備わる (preparedness and innate endowment, positive; slightly utilitarian in 設備/警備); ZH: 具備/完備 (complete, well-prepared)
notes: Theme: Steadfast waiting & constancy (Live-test engine top choice). Elevates 備 from logistical 'preparation' to Mencius's joyful inner completeness (備わる).

meaning_in_line: to mend, compose, and care for attentively (no verified kanji line)
person_quality: patient, restorative care that mends what is worn and tends to relationships with quiet respect
sense_check: No verified kanji line; classical kanji occurrences describe repairing buildings rather than human care, so line_original is left empty per the no-weak-line rule.
context_check: none — no verified person-centered classical line where 繕 is written in kanji; kept with empty line_original per the no-weak-line rule.
standalone_reading_risk: JP: 繕う can mean 'mend clothes/repair' (positive craft) or 'keep up appearances/cover up' (体裁を繕う, negative); ZH: 修繕 (repair). Always pair with the classical card text so the restorative 'mending/making whole with care' sense shines
notes: no verified line — warm person-centered classical uses (such as 徒然草 37段『我に心をきひきつくろへるさまに見ゆるこそ…よき人かなとぞおぼゆる』) write つくろふ in kana, while kanji occurrences describe repairing walls or buildings; see companion kana_only: yes row.

meaning_in_line: to compose and tend to one's bearing with respectful care even with close companions
person_quality: thoughtful courtesy and care that never takes even the closest relationships for granted
line_original: 「朝夕へだてなくなれたる人の、ともある時に、我に心をきひきつくろへるさまに見ゆるこそ、今さらかくやは」などいふ人もありぬべけれど、なほげにげにしくよき人かなとぞおぼゆる。
source: 吉田兼好『徒然草』第三十七段（鎌倉・南北朝時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: ひきつくろへる here means thoughtfully composing one's bearing out of respect for a close companion, matching the gift-card sense of attentive care (written in kana).
context_check: positive — praising someone who, even with an intimate companion seen morning and evening, still tends their bearing with respectful care (ひきつくろへる = 引き繕へる) on occasion, calling them 'a truly admirable person' (よき人かな)
standalone_reading_risk: JP: 繕う ('mend/tend' vs. 'keep up appearances'); requires the Tsurezuregusa story context
notes: Theme: Steadfast waiting & constancy (Secondary reference row marked kana_only: yes, as 引き繕へる is written in hiragana ひきつくろへる in the Kokubun Taikan edition).

meaning_in_line: to stitch together and weave words or fabric with care (no verified kanji line)
person_quality: patient hands and storytelling heart that mend what is frayed and weave small moments into lasting warmth
sense_check: No verified kanji line; classical kanji occurrences describe fruit or prose prefaces rather than human care, so line_original is left empty per the no-weak-line rule.
context_check: none — no verified person-centered classical poem where 綴 is written in kanji; kept with empty line_original per the no-weak-line rule.
standalone_reading_risk: none in JP (綴る means both 'to stitch/bind together' and 'to compose words/memories', warmly poetic); ZH: 點綴 (to adorn/embellish) or 連綴 (to link together), positive
notes: no verified line — warm person-centered classical uses (such as おくのほそ道『もゝひきの破れをつゞり』) write つづる in kana, while kanji occurrences describe fruit or prose prefaces; see companion kana_only: yes row.

meaning_in_line: to stitch and mend worn cloth together for the road ahead
person_quality: patient hands and storytelling heart that mend what is frayed and prepare lovingly for the journey ahead
line_original: もゝひきの破れをつゞり笠の緖付かへて三里に灸すゆるより松島の月先心にかゝりて
source: 松尾芭蕉『おくのほそ道』旅立ち（江戸時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: つゞり here means patiently stitching and mending worn travel clothes for the journey ahead, matching the gift-card sense of patient mending and preparation (written in kana).
context_check: positive — iconic opening of Oku no Hosomichi, mending torn trousers (つゞり = 綴り) and replacing hat cords in eager anticipation of the moon over Matsushima
standalone_reading_risk: none
notes: Theme: Steadfast waiting & constancy (Secondary reference row marked kana_only: yes, as 綴り is written つゞり in the original text).

meaning_in_line: to tie together in a vow of shared life and safety
person_quality: bringing people and promises together into lasting, trustworthy bonds
line_original: 君之齒母 吾代毛所知哉 磐代乃 岡之草根乎 去来結手名
source: 『万葉集』巻一・10 中皇命（飛鳥時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 結 here means tying a vow of shared life and safe return, matching the gift-card sense of uniting hearts in lasting bonds.
context_check: positive — auspicious ritual poem ('君が代も我が代も知るや岩代の岡の草根をいざ結びてな') tying living grass on the hill of Iwashiro to bless both the companion's life and the speaker's life
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 結ぶ and ZH 結緣/團結 celebrate bonding, fruitfulness, and connection; also attested in 『和漢朗詠集』白居易「晩蘂尚開紅躑躅。秋房初結白芙蓉」)
notes: Theme: Steadfast waiting & constancy. 結 appears directly in kanji in the original Man'yoshu text (去来結手名).

meaning_in_line: steadfastly true to principle rather than rigid in petty promises
person_quality: principled integrity that stays true to what is right with wisdom and flexibility
line_original: 子曰：「君子貞而不諒。」
source: 『論語』衞靈公第十五（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 貞 here means staying true to core principle with wisdom, matching the gift-card sense of principled integrity.
context_check: positive — Confucius distinguishing true moral constancy (貞) from blind, stubborn adherence to minor words (諒)
standalone_reading_risk: JP/ZH caution: in modern compounds (貞操, 貞淑, 貞節), 貞 can sound like archaic female chastity moralism. Use only when framed via Confucius's gender-neutral integrity ('貞而不諒') or 『周易』「元亨利貞」
notes: Theme: Steadfast waiting & constancy. Rated card_fit: medium due to modern gendered connotations of 貞操/貞淑; restrict to classical/philosophical contexts.

meaning_in_line: to remain alive and present in the heart across any distance
person_quality: abiding presence and true friendship that makes even the ends of the earth feel like next door
line_original: 海內存知己，天涯若比隣。
source: 王勃「杜少府之任蜀州」唐
sense_check: Confirms match: 存 here means a true friend remaining alive and present in one's heart across any distance, matching the gift-card sense of abiding presence.
context_check: positive — famously bright, uplifting farewell poem rejecting tearful sorrow in favor of the enduring bond between true friends across distance
standalone_reading_risk: none (JP 存じる/存在 and ZH 心存/長存 are dignified; for memorials, 'remaining present in the world/heart' is deeply comforting)
notes: Theme: Steadfast waiting & constancy / Memorial. A premier gift character for long-distance friends, colleagues, and memorials.

meaning_in_line: to trust and lean upon a mother's words across the long years
person_quality: steadfast reliability and trustworthy guidance that loved ones can lean on through every season of life
line_original: たらちねの母の命の言にあらば年の緒長く頼み過ぎむや
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第九・1774 柿本人麻呂歌集（舎人皇子に献れる歌・奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 頼み here means trusting and leaning upon a mother's words through the long years, matching the gift-card sense of steadfast reliability.
context_check: positive — affectionate poem from the Kakinomoto no Hitomaro Kashu invoking the deep, enduring trust placed in a mother's words across the long thread of years (年の緒長く頼み); also celebrated in 『枕草子』where Fujiwara no Michitaka rewrites the end of a famous waka as 「君をばふかくたのむはやわが」to great acclaim
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 頼る/頼もしい/信頼 and ZH 信賴/倚賴 express warm, dependable trust)
notes: Theme: Steadfast waiting & constancy (Phase 2 Japanese classical expansion). 頼み appears directly in kanji in Kamochi Masazumi's Man'yoshu edition.

meaning_in_line: to think fondly and tenderly of someone dear when the cherry blossoms bloom in spring
person_quality: enduring, tender remembrance that holds a cherished person close in every season
line_original: 絶等寸の山の峰の上の桜花咲かむ春へは君し偲はむ
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第九・1776 播磨娘子（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 偲はむ here means thinking fondly and tenderly of a cherished person when the cherry blossoms bloom, matching the gift-card sense of loving remembrance.
context_check: positive — warm farewell poem promising that whenever spring comes and the cherry blossoms bloom on the mountain peak, the speaker will fondly remember and cherish you (桜花咲かむ春へは君し偲はむ); also written logographically in 『万葉集』巻一・66「大伴乃 高師能濱乃 松之根乎 枕宿杼 家之所偲由」
standalone_reading_risk: JP: 偲ぶ (しのぶ, 'to remember fondly/cherish in memory' — unlike 忍ぶ, 偲ぶ has the person radical 亻 and means exclusively tender remembrance and appreciation, never 'enduring pain' or 'hiding'); ZH: 偲 in classical Chinese (『詩經・齊風・盧令』「盧令令，其人美且偲」) means 'talented and sincere'. Ideal for memorials and cherished mentors/friends
notes: Theme: Memorial & Steadfast remembrance (Phase 2 Japanese classical expansion). Unlike 忍 (excluded due to 忍耐/我慢), 偲 (person radical + 思) is pure, warm remembrance in Japanese and 'admirable/talented' in the Book of Odes.

meaning_in_line: to observe deeply what brings a person's heart peace
person_quality: perceptive empathy that notices what truly makes someone feel at home without needing to be told
line_original: 子曰：「視其所以，觀其所由，察其所安，人焉廋哉！人焉廋哉！」
source: 『論語』為政第二（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 察 here means observing deeply what brings another person's heart peace, matching the gift-card sense of perceptive empathy.
context_check: positive — Confucius explaining progressive depth of understanding a person: looking at their actions, seeing their path, and discerning where their heart finds peace (察其所安)
standalone_reading_risk: JP: 察する ('to sense/empathize with another's feelings without words' — one of the highest virtues in Japanese culture); minor compound overlap with 警察/観察. ZH: 明察/體察 (perceptive, considerate)
notes: Theme: Quiet understanding (Live-test engine top choice). 「察其所安」is the ideal classical anchor for Japanese 察する.

meaning_in_line: to honor and treat others with genuine respect
person_quality: steady, heartfelt respect toward every person and task, inspiring mutual reverence
fits_relationships: mentor / parent / partner / work / friend / memorial
line_original: 仁者愛人，有禮者敬人。愛人者，人恒愛之；敬人者，人恒敬之。
source: 『孟子』離婁下（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 敬 here means honoring others with genuine, consistent respect, matching the gift-card sense of heartfelt reverence.
context_check: positive — Mencius affirming how benevolence and respect naturally reciprocate in human relationships
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 敬う/敬意 and ZH 敬重/尊敬 are universally noble and positive; also supported by 『論語・學而』「敬事而信」)
notes: Theme: Quiet understanding. Combines interpersonal reverence (孟子「有禮者敬人」) with professional dedication (論語「敬事而信」).

meaning_in_line: empathetic reciprocity and forgiving consideration for others
person_quality: lifelong empathy that measures others' struggles with a gentle, understanding heart
line_original: 子貢問曰：「有一言而可以終身行之者乎？」子曰：「其恕乎！己所不欲，勿施於人。」
source: 『論語』衞靈公第十五（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 恕 here means lifelong empathetic reciprocity and consideration for others' feelings, matching the gift-card sense of forgiving understanding.
context_check: positive — Confucius directly answering the question 'Is there one single character (一言) to practice for a whole lifetime?' with 恕
standalone_reading_risk: JP: 恕す (ゆるす, to forgive/empathize; literary and noble); ZH: 寬恕 (forgive, positive, though standalone 恕 in modern ZH appears in polite apologies like 恕不遠送). The Analects 'one character for life' story makes it extraordinary for ICHIREI
notes: Theme: Quiet understanding. Literally Confucius's own 'one-kanji gift' (一言而可以終身行之者) to Zigong.

meaning_in_line: serenely still, grounded, and unshaken like a mountain
person_quality: calm, mountain-like composure that brings peace and clarity to everyone nearby
line_original: 子曰：「知者樂水，仁者樂山。知者動，仁者靜。知者樂，仁者壽。」
source: 『論語』雍也第六（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 靜 here means the serene, mountain-like stillness of a benevolent person, matching the gift-card sense of grounded calm.
context_check: positive — celebrating the complementary virtues of the wise and the benevolent, linking the stillness of the benevolent person (仁者靜) with longevity and mountain-like stability
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 静か/静けさ and ZH 寧靜/沉靜 are serene and positive; unlike 黙, 靜/静 carries no rude imperative connotation)
notes: Theme: Quiet understanding. Kyujitai 靜; see companion Shinjitai 静 row in 『和漢朗詠集』.

meaning_in_line: serenely calm in heart, bringing refreshing coolness even in summer heat
person_quality: serene inner composure that stays cool, unruffled, and refreshing amid the heat and hurry of life
line_original: 不是禅房無熱到。但能心静即身涼。
source: 『和漢朗詠集』巻上・夏・納涼 白居易「苦熱題恒寂禅師房」（唐・平安撰）
sense_check: Confirms match: 心静 here means serene inner calm that brings refreshing peace amid heat and bustle, matching the gift-card sense of tranquil composure.
context_check: positive — famous couplet in Wakan Roeishu ('是れ禅房に熱の到ること無きあらず、たゞ能く心静かなれば即ち身も涼し', origin of the Japanese proverb 心頭滅却すれば火もまた涼し / 心静かなれば身も涼し)
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 静か and ZH 寧靜 are wholly positive; recommended replacement for 黙)
notes: Theme: Quiet understanding (Japanese anthology companion row for Shinjitai 静).

meaning_in_line: unhurriedly, at ease, and in natural harmony with the world
person_quality: spacious, unhurried spirit that stays free from worldly rush and sees beauty clearly
line_original: 採菊東籬下，悠然見南山。
source: 陶淵明「飲酒二十首（其五）」東晉
sense_check: Confirms match: 悠然 here means unhurried, spacious ease of spirit in harmony with nature, matching the gift-card sense of unhurried grace.
context_check: positive — iconic poem of inner peace and spiritual freedom amidst nature, concluding that true meaning lies beyond words ('此中有真意，欲辨已忘言')
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 悠々/悠然 and ZH 悠然/悠久 evoke spacious calm and timelessness; anchor specifically in Tao Yuanming's 悠然見南山)
notes: Theme: Quiet understanding. One of East Asia's most beloved lines for someone retiring, living authentically, or cherished for their calm presence.

meaning_in_line: to strive after and embody true sincerity
person_quality: wholehearted authenticity and truthfulness without a trace of pretense
fits_relationships: partner / parent / mentor / friend / work / memorial
line_original: 誠者，天之道也；誠之者，人之道也。
source: 『禮記』中庸・第二十章（先秦・秦漢）
sense_check: Confirms match: 誠 here means wholehearted sincerity and truthfulness as the human way, matching the gift-card sense of authentic sincerity.
context_check: positive — philosophical pinnacle of the Doctrine of the Mean, defining sincerity both as the way of Heaven and the active verb ('to make it real / strive for sincerity', 誠之) of human life
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 誠/誠実 and ZH 真誠/誠懇 are among the highest moral compliments in both languages; also in 『万葉集』巻五 吉田宜書簡「宜戀主之誠」)
notes: Theme: Quiet understanding. In 「誠之者」, 誠 functions dynamically as a verb ('to make sincere / to realize sincerity in action').

meaning_in_line: deeply devoted, warm, and earnest toward family and kin
person_quality: deep-rooted devotion and earnest follow-through that inspires trust in everyone around them
line_original: 君子篤於親，則民興於仁。故舊不遺，則民不偷。
source: 『論語』泰伯第八（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 篤 here means deep, earnest devotion toward family and kin, matching the gift-card sense of warm, steadfast follow-through.
context_check: positive — Master Zeng (曾子) teaching that when a noble person is deeply devoted to kin and never forsakes old friends, the whole community rises in benevolence
standalone_reading_risk: JP caution: while 篤実/懇篤/篤志 are noble, 危篤 means 'critically ill'. Never give to someone who is hospitalized or frail; for healthy recipients or『中庸』「篤行之」, it is noble
notes: Theme: Quiet understanding. Also appears as an adverb in 『禮記・中庸』「篤行之」. Restricted against ill/hospitalized recipients.

meaning_in_line: to grow mild and harmonize gently in the early spring air
person_quality: warm, harmonizing presence that eases tension and brings people closer together like a spring breeze
line_original: 時に初春の令月、気淑く風和ぐ。梅は鏡前の粉を披き、蘭は珮後の香を薫らす。
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第五・815 梅花歌卅二首并序（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 和ぐ here means softening and harmonizing gently like the early spring breeze, matching the gift-card sense of warm harmony.
context_check: positive — the famous Dazaifu plum-blossom banquet preface (source of the Reiwa era name; original kanbun in 万葉集/第五巻: 「于時初春令月 氣淑風和梅披鏡前之粉 蘭薫珮後之香」), celebrating gentle harmony and fellowship
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 和む/和らげる/平和 and ZH 溫和/和諧 are universally auspicious; also supported by 『論語・學而』「禮之用，和為貴」and 『和漢朗詠集』章孝標「梅花帯雪飛琴上。柳色和煙入酒中」)
notes: Theme: Quiet understanding (Revised in v2: upgraded primary row to the Man'yoshu Plum Blossom Preface where 和 appears directly in kanji in both the original kanbun and Kamochi Masazumi's kundoku edition).

meaning_in_line: to soften hearts and bring people into gentle harmony
person_quality: empathetic warmth that effortlessly softens distance between hearts
line_original: ちからをもいれずしてあめつちをうごかし、めに見えぬおにかみをもあはれとおもはせ、をとこをむなのなかをもやはらげ、たけきものゝふのこゝろをもなぐさむるはうたなり。
source: 紀貫之『古今和歌集仮名序』（平安時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: やはらげ here means softening hearts and bringing people into gentle harmony, matching the gift-card sense of empathetic peacemaking (written in kana).
context_check: positive — famous opening manifesto of Japanese poetics celebrating how poetry softens (やはらげ = 和らげ) relationships between men and women
standalone_reading_risk: none
notes: Theme: Quiet understanding (Secondary reference row marked kana_only: yes, as 和らげ is written in hiragana やはらげ in the Kana Preface).

meaning_in_line: broad-minded, magnanimous, and unhurried in spirit
person_quality: generous breadth of heart that gives others room to breathe while staying grounded in dignity
line_original: 直而溫，寬而栗，剛而無虐，簡而無傲。
source: 『尚書』虞書・舜典（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 寬 (寛) here means broad-minded magnanimity paired with dignity, matching the gift-card sense of generous breadth of heart.
context_check: positive — Emperor Shun's foundational charter on educating the youth through balanced virtues: upright yet warm, broad-minded yet reverent (寬而栗)
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 寛ぐ/寛大/寛容 and ZH 寬厚/寬容 are warm and generous; also supported by 『周易・乾卦・文言』「寬以居之，仁以行之」)
notes: Theme: Quiet understanding (Live-test engine top choice). Shinjitai 寛 corresponds to Traditional 寬 in the Chinese source text.

meaning_in_line: to be serenely clear and tranquil, cradling floating lotus leaves
person_quality: serene, unclouded clarity of heart that holds everyone around it in peaceful calm
line_original: はすのうき葉のらうたげにてのどかに澄める池のおもてにおほきなるとちひさきとひろごりたゞよひてありくいとをかし。
source: 清少納言『枕草子』（國文大觀本）「草は」（平安時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 澄める here means serene, unclouded clarity that cradles floating lotus leaves in peace, matching the gift-card sense of clear-hearted calm.
context_check: positive — affectionate observation in The Pillow Book delighting in endearing lotus leaves, large and small, drifting across the surface of a serenely clear pond (のどかに澄める池のおもてに)
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 澄む/澄み切る and ZH 澄明/清澈 are pure, luminous, and tranquil; also attested in 王維「青谿」『漾漾泛菱荇，澄澄映葭葦。我心素已閒，清川澹如此』)
notes: Theme: Quiet understanding (Revised in v2: upgraded primary row to Makura no Soshi where 澄める is written directly in kanji, plus Wang Wei's 青谿; kept Basho's おくのほそ道 line as secondary kana_only: yes row).

meaning_in_line: to become clear, tranquil, and transparent in heart
person_quality: crystalline clarity of mind and spirit that quiets the noise of the world
line_original: 佳景寂寞として心すみ行のみ覺ゆ
source: 松尾芭蕉『おくのほそ道』立石寺（江戸時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 心すみ行 here means the heart becoming crystal-clear and tranquil, matching the gift-card sense of inner clarity (written in kana).
context_check: positive — contemplative stillness at Ryushakuji where the traveler feels his heart growing progressively clearer and calmer (心すみ行のみ覺ゆ)
standalone_reading_risk: none
notes: Theme: Quiet understanding (Secondary reference row marked kana_only: yes, as 澄み行く is written すみ行 in the original text).

meaning_in_line: to understand and recognize another's true heart and intention
person_quality: deep, unspoken understanding that recognizes and honors another person's true heart
line_original: 若使韶光知我意。今宵旅宿在詩家。
source: 『和漢朗詠集』巻上・春・三月尽 菅原道真「送春」（平安時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 知 here means deeply understanding and recognizing another's true heart (我意), matching the gift-card sense of unspoken understanding.
context_check: positive — Sugawara no Michizane's affectionate poem to spring light ('若し韶光をして我が意を知らしめば、今宵の旅宿は詩家に在らん': if the radiant spring light knows my heart, tonight it will lodge in the poet's home); also grounded in 『論語・為政』「溫故而知新，可以為師矣」
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 知る/知己 and ZH 知音/知己 are deeply affirming when anchored in 'one who truly knows')
notes: Theme: Quiet understanding (Revised in v2: upgraded primary row to Sugawara no Michizane in Wakan Roeishu where 知 appears directly in kanji, while retaining Ki no Tomonori's Kokinshu 38 waka as secondary kana_only: yes row).

meaning_in_line: to truly recognize and appreciate both the beauty and the inner fragrance of another
person_quality: irreplaceable understanding — being the one person who truly sees and treasures who you are
line_original: 君ならて誰にか見せむ梅花色をもかをもしる人そしる
source: 『古今和歌集』巻一・春歌上・38 紀友則（平安時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: しる here means truly recognizing and appreciating another person's inner worth, matching the gift-card sense of irreplaceable understanding (written in kana).
context_check: positive — celebrated waka sending a branch of plum blossoms to a cherished person ('If not to you, to whom would I show these plum blossoms? Only one who truly knows can appreciate both their color and their fragrance')
standalone_reading_risk: none
notes: Theme: Quiet understanding (Secondary reference row marked kana_only: yes, as 知る is written しる in the Kokinshu text; also appears in 『和漢朗詠集』巻上・紅梅 as 「君ならでたれにかみせんうめのはないろをもかをもしる人ぞしる」).

meaning_in_line: upright, unbending, and open-centered in integrity
person_quality: honest, unpretentious integrity that rises clean and straight from any environment
line_original: 予獨愛蓮之出淤泥而不染，濯清漣而不妖，中通外直，不蔓不枝，香遠益清，亭亭淨植，可遠觀而不可褻玩焉。
source: 周敦頤「愛蓮說」北宋
sense_check: Confirms match: 直 here means upright, unbending moral integrity that stays pure in any environment, matching the gift-card sense of honest straightforwardness.
context_check: positive — classic prose tribute to the lotus as the symbol of the noble person (君子) whose inner openness and outer uprightness (中通外直) spread fragrance far and wide
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP まっすぐ/素直/実直 and ZH 正直/率直 are bright, honest, and admirable; also supported by 『尚書・舜典』「直而溫」)
notes: Theme: Strength & endurance in a bright form. Pairing 直 with 周敦頤「中通外直」or 『尚書』「直而溫」ensures it reads as warm integrity rather than bluntness.

meaning_in_line: with dignified, unbending integrity and clear-eyed poise
person_quality: dignified, upright poise and inner integrity that stands tall and uncompromised
line_original: 凜然相對敢相欺，直幹淩空未要奇。根到九泉無曲處，世間惟有蟄龍知。
source: 蘇軾「王復秀才所居雙檜（其二）」北宋
sense_check: Confirms match: 凜然 here means dignified, uncompromised moral poise rising straight toward the sky, matching the gift-card sense of dignified integrity.
context_check: positive — Su Shi praises Scholar Wang Fu's noble, unbending character through the twin evergreen cypresses at his home, which face each other with dignified integrity (凜然相對), rise straight into the sky (直幹淩空), and have roots without a single crooked bend; completely free of 老 or 秋 and auspicious for 還暦.
standalone_reading_risk: JP: 凛とした/凛々しい (universally admired in modern Japan for dignified, graceful strength); ZH: 凜然 (dignified, awe-inspiring poise) vs. 凜冽 (biting cold). Anchoring in Su Shi's 「凜然不知秋」eliminates the 'icy cold' sense
notes: Replaces earlier Su Shi poem containing 老 and 秋. Here 凜然 describes dignified moral poise (not icy cold) and evergreen cypresses (雙檜), making it safe and celebratory for 60th-birthday (還暦) and mentor gifts.

meaning_in_line: firm, unyielding in moral spine, and free of self-interest
person_quality: quiet, unshakeable backbone that needs no boastful words to prove its strength
line_original: 子曰：「剛毅木訥，近仁。」
source: 『論語』子路第十三（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 剛 here means quiet, unyielding moral backbone close to benevolence, matching the gift-card sense of inner strength.
context_check: positive — Confucius linking firm resolve, endurance, simplicity, and modest speech directly to benevolence (仁)
standalone_reading_risk: JP/ZH: 剛直/剛健 (strong, upright); minor risk of sounding hard or rigid if isolated, which 『論語』「剛毅木訥，近仁」and 『尚書』「剛而無虐」soften into humane strength
notes: Theme: Strength & endurance in a bright form. Links firmness of character (剛) directly to benevolence (仁).

meaning_in_line: supple gentleness and life-giving flexibility
person_quality: gentle, resilient adaptability that overcomes the hardest obstacles without force
line_original: 專氣致柔，能如嬰兒乎？
source: 『老子』道德經・第十章（唐玄宗御註本・先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 柔 here means supple, life-giving gentleness of spirit, matching the gift-card sense of resilient gentleness.
context_check: positive — Daoist meditation on concentrating vital breath to attain the supple, vital softness of a newborn child (also 『禮記・中庸』「寬裕溫柔，足以有容也」)
standalone_reading_risk: JP: 柔らかい/柔軟 (gentle, flexible, positive; avoid 優柔不断); ZH: 溫柔/柔韌 (tender and resilient)
notes: Theme: Strength & endurance in a bright form. In Laozi and Zhongyong, 柔 is the supple strength of life and warmth.

meaning_in_line: resilient, sinewy, and unyielding against the gale
person_quality: spirited resilience that stands even taller and clearer when the winds of adversity blow
line_original: 風聲一何盛，松枝一何勁！
source: 劉楨「贈從弟三首（其二・亭亭山上松）」漢・建安
sense_check: Confirms match: 勁 here means resilient strength that stands firm against the fiercest wind, matching the gift-card sense of spirited endurance.
context_check: positive — encouraging poem to his cousin praising the mountain pine whose branches show their true, vigorous strength against the wind
standalone_reading_risk: none (JP 強い/勁い is a refined literary kanji for resilient strength; ZH 蒼勁/強勁/有勁 is energetic, vital, and positive; also famous in 鄭燮「竹石」『千磨萬擊還堅勁』)
notes: Theme: Strength & endurance in a bright form. Supported both by Liu Zhen's pine poem and Zheng Xie's bamboo poem.

meaning_in_line: resolute, steadfast, and capable of holding firm to purpose
person_quality: unwavering inner resolve paired with warmth and breadth of heart
line_original: 唯天下至聖，為能聰明叡知，足以有臨也；寬裕溫柔，足以有容也；發強剛毅，足以有執也；
source: 『禮記』中庸・第三十一章（先秦・秦漢）
sense_check: Confirms match: 毅 here means resolute, unwavering perseverance paired with warmth of heart, matching the gift-card sense of steadfast resolve.
context_check: positive — celebrating the harmony of gentle warmth (寬裕溫柔) and resolute, dynamic fortitude (發強剛毅) in a great person, completely free of any death imagery
standalone_reading_risk: none for standalone kanji (JP 毅然 and ZH 堅毅/弘毅 are noble); IMPORTANT LINE CAUTION: never print the full 『論語・泰伯』8.7 quote「死而後已」on 還暦, birthday, or memorial cards (if quoting Analects 8.7, stop at「士不可以不弘毅，任重而道遠」)
notes: Theme: Strength & endurance in a bright form (Revised in v2: replaced Analects 8.7「死而後已」with Zhongyong 31「發強剛毅」so the card quote is 100% safe for 還暦, birthdays, and retirements).

meaning_in_line: vigorously, tirelessly in motion like the heavens
person_quality: bright, tireless vitality that renews itself day after day without ever losing heart
line_original: 乾：天行健，君子以自強不息。
source: 『周易』大象・乾卦（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 健 here means tireless, self-renewing vitality like the movement of heaven, matching the gift-card sense of bright, healthy vigor.
context_check: positive — the opening hexagram statement of the I Ching, celebrating cosmic vitality and unceasing self-cultivation
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 健やか/健気 and ZH 康健/剛健 are warm, auspicious, and life-affirming)
notes: Theme: Strength & endurance in a bright form. Bridges cosmic strength (天行健) with everyday Japanese warmth (健やか / 健気).

meaning_in_line: uncarved wood; natural, unadorned genuineness
person_quality: earthy, unpretentious authenticity that stays true to its original grain like uncarved wood
line_original: 見素抱樸，少私寡欲。
source: 『老子』道德經・第十九章（唐玄宗御註本・先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 樸 here means unadorned, natural genuineness like uncarved wood, matching the gift-card sense of humble authenticity.
context_check: positive — Laozi's call to behold raw silk and embrace the uncarved block (抱樸), returning to genuine simplicity and warmth
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 素朴/朴訥 and ZH 淳樸/質樸 praise honest, unpretentious character; note JP Joyo uses 朴 while Traditional/literary uses 樸)
notes: Theme: Strength & endurance in a bright form. Especially poetic for ICHIREI because the gift itself is carved in wood, honoring the recipient's natural 'uncarved grain' (樸).

meaning_in_line: serenely poised, magnanimous, and free from arrogance
person_quality: calm, grounded self-assurance that puts others at ease without ever boasting
line_original: 子曰：「君子泰而不驕；小人驕而不泰。」
source: 『論語』子路第十三（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 泰 here means calm, magnanimous poise free of arrogance, matching the gift-card sense of composed assurance.
context_check: positive — Confucius contrasting true, spacious composure (泰) with brittle arrogance (驕)
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 泰然/安泰 and ZH 泰然/國泰民安 are auspicious, calm, and dignified)
notes: Theme: Strength & endurance in a bright form. An exceptional character for calm leaders and elders.

meaning_in_line: earnest, nimble, and decisive in action
person_quality: quietly capable action that speaks through deeds rather than boastful words
line_original: 子曰：「君子欲訥於言而敏於行。」
source: 『論語』里仁第四（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 敏 here means earnest, capable readiness in action rather than boastful words, matching the gift-card sense of quiet capability.
context_check: positive — Confucius praising the person who is modest and measured in speech yet swift and earnest in action
standalone_reading_risk: JP/ZH: 機敏/敏腕 (capable, sharp) vs. 敏感/過敏 ('sensitive/allergic' in modern everyday compounds). Pairing with「訥於言而敏於行」makes the meaning unmistakably 'earnest in action'
notes: Theme: Strength & endurance in a bright form. Ideal for someone who quietly gets things done without seeking the spotlight.

meaning_in_line: safely, blessedly, and in good health and fortune
person_quality: warm blessing and joyful presence that brings happiness and safe passage to those they love
line_original: 竹玉を 繁に貫き垂り 斎瓮に 木綿取り垂でて 斎ひつつ 吾が 思ふ 吾子 ま幸くありこそ
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第九・1790 遣唐使の親母が子に贈れる歌（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: ま幸く here means a mother's prayer for her child's safe, blessed well-being, matching the gift-card sense of warm blessing and happiness.
context_check: positive — a mother's heartfelt prayer for her beloved child setting sail, stringing bamboo jewels and hanging sacred bark-cloth to pray: 'May my beloved child be ever safe and blessed!' (吾が思ふ吾子ま幸くありこそ); also in 9・1668「白崎は幸くあり待て大船に真梶繁貫きまたかへり見む」
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 幸い/幸せ/さきく and ZH 幸福/慶幸 are universally auspicious and warm)
notes: Theme: Care & nurture / Blessing (Phase 2 Japanese classical expansion). ま幸くありこそ appears directly in kanji in Kamochi Masazumi's Man'yoshu edition.

meaning_in_line: to shine clearly through the pines and illuminate
person_quality: clear, steady light that brightens the path and brings peace to those in the shadows
line_original: 明月松間照，清泉石上流。
source: 王維「山居秋暝」唐
sense_check: Confirms match: 照 here means clear, steady moonlight illuminating the pines, matching the gift-card sense of radiant guidance and warmth.
context_check: positive — luminous, tranquil portrait of an autumn evening in the mountains after rain, celebrating pure nature and peaceful community
standalone_reading_risk: none (JP 照らす/照る and ZH 照亮/關照 are warm and luminous; JP 照れる 'to feel shy' is endearing rather than negative)
notes: Theme: Light & warmth (Priority character). Validated across both Chinese (王維「明月松間照」) and Japanese (see companion Makura no Soshi row below) classics.

meaning_in_line: to shine warmly and serenely across the spring courtyard
person_quality: serene, spring-like radiance that warms the whole household and brings music to life
line_original: 二月十日の日のうらうらと長閑に照り渡るに、わたどのゝ雨の廂にてうへ 〈一條院〉の御笛ふかせ給ふ。
source: 清少納言『枕草子』（國文大觀本）「小一條院をば今內裏とぞいふ」（平安時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 照り渡る here means spring sunlight shining warmly and serenely across the household, matching the gift-card sense of warm, radiant presence.
context_check: positive — idyllic spring scene in The Pillow Book where the tenth-day sun of the second month shines warmly and serenely across the garden (うらうらと長閑に照り渡るに) while the Emperor plays the flute in duet; also in 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』9・1753「筑波嶺を さやに照らして」
standalone_reading_risk: none
notes: Theme: Light & warmth (Japanese classical primary companion row for 照, where 照り渡るに appears directly in kanji).

meaning_in_line: warm, genial, and approachable in countenance and spirit
person_quality: gentle warmth of character that makes people feel welcomed, safe, and respected
fits_relationships: parent / partner / mentor / friend / work / memorial
line_original: 夫子溫、良、恭、儉、讓以得之。夫子之求之也，其諸異乎人之求之與！
source: 『論語』學而第一（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 溫 here means gentle, approachable warmth of character, matching the gift-card sense of comforting human warmth.
context_check: positive — Zigong describing why people in every state gladly shared their heart with Confucius: not through demand, but through his warmth (溫), kindness, respect, frugality, and humility
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 温かい/温和 and ZH 溫和/溫暖 are universally cherished; also appears as a verb 'to warm up / revisit with care' in 『論語・為政』「溫故而知新」)
notes: Theme: Light & warmth. Dual classical power: adjective of personal warmth in Analects 1.10 and active verb ('cherishing/revisiting the old') in Analects 2.11 (Kyujitai 溫 / Shinjitai 温).

meaning_in_line: deep, generous, and capacious in virtue
person_quality: deep-rooted generosity and trustworthiness capable of supporting everyone and everything around them
fits_relationships: parent / partner / mentor / friend / work / memorial
line_original: 坤：地勢坤，君子以厚德載物。
source: 『周易』大象・坤卦（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 厚 here means deep, generous virtue capable of supporting all things, matching the gift-card sense of deep-rooted kindness.
context_check: positive — the companion statement to 天行健, praising the earth-like depth of virtue that holds and supports all living things (also in 『万葉集』巻五 藤原房前書簡「乃知 龍門之恩復厚蓬身之上」)
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 厚い/温厚/重厚 and ZH 寬厚/深厚/厚道 are warm, substantial, and deeply positive; also attested in 『論語・學而』「愼終追遠，民德歸厚矣」 for memorials)
notes: Theme: Light & warmth. Ideal for both living pillars of a family/team (『周易』「厚德載物」) and memorial tributes (『論語』「愼終追遠，民德歸厚矣」).

meaning_in_line: an enduring lamp of wisdom and compassion held aloft
person_quality: quiet, unwavering guiding light that keeps hope and wisdom alive for others
line_original: 天台止觀の月明らかに圓頓融通の法の灯かゝげそひて僧坊棟をならべ修驗行法をはげまし
source: 松尾芭蕉『おくのほそ道』出羽三山（江戸時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 灯 here means an enduring lamp of wisdom and compassion held aloft for others, matching the gift-card sense of a guiding light.
context_check: positive — reverent praise of the spiritual tradition at Dewa Sanzan, where the clear moon of contemplation shines and the lamp of the Dharma (法の灯) is held aloft across generations
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP ともしび/灯す and ZH 明灯/點灯 symbolize warmth, guidance, and continuity in the dark)
notes: Theme: Light & warmth / Memorial (Priority character). 灯 appears directly in kanji in 『おくのほそ道』「法の灯かゝげそひて」.

meaning_in_line: a warm solitary lamp beside which one communes with timeless friends
person_quality: warm, companionable light that turns solitude into comfort and deep conversation
line_original: ひとり燈のもとに文をひろげて、見ぬ人を友とするこそこよなう慰むわざなれ。
source: 吉田兼好『徒然草』第十三段（鎌倉・南北朝時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 燈 here means a warm lamp beside which one communes with cherished friends in the heart, matching the gift-card sense of companionable warmth.
context_check: positive — beloved reflection on the supreme comfort of opening a book beneath a lamp and befriending wise souls of the past
standalone_reading_risk: none (Kyujitai/Traditional 燈 carries classic literary elegance in both JP and ZH)
notes: Theme: Light & warmth / Memorial. Particularly resonant for book lovers, teachers, scholars, and memorials ('befriending someone unseen beneath the lamp').

meaning_in_line: to brighten, illuminate, and bring radiant virtue to light
person_quality: radiant clarity and optimism that brings out the brightest qualities in everyone around them
fits_relationships: partner / parent / mentor / friend / child / work
line_original: 大學之道，在明明德，在親民，在止於至善。
source: 『禮記』大學（先秦・秦漢）
sense_check: Confirms match: 明 here means illuminating and bringing radiant virtue to light, matching the gift-card sense of bright, uplifting clarity.
context_check: positive — the opening sentence of the Great Learning, where the first 明 is an active verb ('to illuminate/make bright') and the second 明 modifies 德 ('luminous virtue'); also in 『万葉集』巻一・15「渡津海乃 豊旗雲尓 伊理比紗之 今夜乃月夜 清明己曽」
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 明るい/明かす and ZH 光明/明朗 are universally bright and auspicious; also in 『枕草子』第一段「春はあけぼの。やうやう白くなりゆく山ぎは少し明りて」)
notes: Theme: Light & warmth. A textbook classical 煉字 where 明 acts as a transitive verb ('to illuminate luminous virtue'), echoed by Man'yoshu 1・15「清明己曽」.

meaning_in_line: crystalline, pure, and continually renewed from a living spring
person_quality: refreshing purity of heart and mind, constantly renewed by curiosity and integrity
line_original: 問渠那得清如許，為有源頭活水來。
source: 朱熹「觀書有感」南宋
sense_check: Confirms match: 清 here means crystalline purity continually renewed from a living spring, matching the gift-card sense of refreshing integrity.
context_check: positive — joyful philosophical poem comparing a clear pond reflecting sky and clouds to a mind kept fresh by a constant inflow of living water
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 清らか/清々しい and ZH 清澈/清朗 are pure and uplifting; also supported by 松尾芭蕉『おくのほそ道』「月淸し遊行のもてる砂の上」)
notes: Theme: Light & warmth. Paired with the Japanese Man'yoshu companion row below.

meaning_in_line: pure, sparkling, and refreshing to behold
person_quality: clear, refreshing integrity of spirit that uplifts everyone who walks beside them
line_original: 大滝を過ぎて夏身にそひ居りて清き川瀬を見るがさやけさ
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第九・1737 兵部川原（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 清き here means pure, sparkling clarity that refreshes the spirit of all who behold it, matching the gift-card sense of refreshing integrity.
context_check: positive — joyful Yoshino poem celebrating staying close beside Natsumi beyond the great falls and beholding the pure, sparkling river rapids (清き川瀬を見るがさやけさ; also in 1・36 柿本人麻呂「山川之 清河内跡」)
standalone_reading_risk: none
notes: Theme: Light & warmth (Japanese classical primary companion row for 清, where 清き appears directly in kanji).

meaning_in_line: to clear away clouds and brighten the spring landscape
person_quality: sunny, cloud-clearing presence that lifts the mood of a room the moment they arrive
line_original: 霞光曙後殷於火。草色晴来嫩似煙。
source: 『和漢朗詠集』巻上・春・霞 白居易「早春晴寄蘇州劉夢得」（唐・平安撰）
sense_check: Confirms match: 晴 here means clouds clearing to reveal fresh, bright spring life, matching the gift-card sense of a sunny, mood-lifting presence.
context_check: positive — vibrant early spring poem celebrating dawn glow redder than fire and young grass turning tender as mist as the sky clears (草の色は晴れ来たりて嫩くして煙に似たり)
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 晴れる/晴れやか/素晴らしい and ZH 晴朗/放晴 are joyful, bright, and celebratory)
notes: Theme: Light & warmth. In Wakan Roeishu, 晴来 (晴れ来たりて) uses 晴 dynamically as an intransitive verb of clearing and brightening.

meaning_in_line: gently warm, coaxing the first blossoms on the southern branch to open
person_quality: gentle, sun-like warmth that quietly encourages closed hearts and new beginnings to blossom
line_original: 誰言春色従東到。露暖南枝花始開。
source: 『和漢朗詠集』巻上・春・梅 菅原文時（平安時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 暖 here means gentle warmth coaxing the first blossoms on the branch to open, matching the gift-card sense of encouraging warmth.
context_check: positive — celebrated Heian kanshi couplet ('誰か言ふ春の色東より到るとは、露暖かにして南枝花始めて開く') showing that spring begins wherever warm dew touches the southern branch
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 暖かい and ZH 溫暖/春暖花開 are wholly positive and comforting)
notes: Theme: Light & warmth. A quintessential poetic eye (詩眼) by Heian scholar-poet Sugawara no Fumitoki where 暖 causes the very first flower of spring to open.

meaning_in_line: fragrant with noble character that spreads far beyond humble walls
person_quality: quiet nobility of character whose warmth and grace fill even the simplest room like fragrance
line_original: 斯是陋室，惟吾德馨。
source: 劉禹錫「陋室銘」唐
sense_check: Confirms match: 馨 here means the lasting fragrance of noble character filling even a humble room, matching the gift-card sense of quiet grace.
context_check: positive — cheerful, proud prose-inscription celebrating a simple home made rich by scholarship, music, nature, and fragrant virtue
standalone_reading_risk: none (JP 馨しい/かぐわしい and ZH 溫馨/德馨 are refined, warm, and deeply complimentary)
notes: Theme: Light & warmth / Memorial. 馨 here acts as a predicate adjective/verb ('is fragrant far and wide').

meaning_in_line: to glow softly and drift through the night like a firefly
person_quality: gentle, unpretentious radiance that brings wonder and reassurance even in the dark
line_original: 闇もなほ螢の多く飛び違ひたる。また、ただ一つ二つなど、ほのかにうち光りて行くもをかし。
source: 清少納言『枕草子』第一段「春はあけぼの」（平安時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 光りて here means glowing softly and reassuringly in the dark, matching the gift-card sense of gentle, hopeful light.
context_check: positive — famous Summer section of the opening passage of The Pillow Book, delighting in both swarms of fireflies and just one or two glowing softly (ほのかにうち光りて行く) in the dark
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 光る/光 and ZH 光芒/陽光 are universally positive)
notes: Theme: Light & warmth. Uses 光 as an active verb (うち光りて = glowing softly), ideal for someone whose quiet presence shines without ostentation.

meaning_in_line: filled with pure gladness and unguarded joy
person_quality: infectiously warm gladness that puts everyone at ease as if they were in their own home
line_original: いふかりし 国のまほらを つばらかに 示したまへば 嬉しみと 紐の緒解きて 家のごと 解けてそ遊ぶ
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第九・1753 高橋虫麻呂歌集（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 嬉しみと here means wholehearted gladness that lets everyone relax as if at home, matching the gift-card sense of infectious joy.
context_check: positive — joyful celebration on Mount Tsukuba where the clouds part to reveal the fair land, and in pure gladness (嬉しみと) everyone unties their cords and relaxes as if at home; also in 19・4273 大納言巨勢朝臣「天地と相栄えむと大宮を仕へまつれば貴く嬉しき」
standalone_reading_risk: none in JP (嬉しい is one of the warmest, most heartfelt everyday Japanese adjectives); ZH: 嬉戲 ('playful/frolicsome' — slightly lighter in ZH than JP, so best for Japanese buyers)
notes: Theme: Light & warmth (Phase 2 Japanese classical expansion). 嬉しみと and 貴く嬉しき appear directly in kanji in Kamochi Masazumi's Man'yoshu edition.

meaning_in_line: to bless and celebrate both one's lord/loved ones and oneself on New Year's morning
person_quality: warm, celebratory spirit that honors milestones and blesses everyone around them
line_original: 正月一日はまいてそらのけしきうらうらとめづらしくかすみこめたるに、世にあるとある人は、すがたかたち心ことにつくろひ、君をも我が身をも祝ひなどしたるさま殊にをかし。
source: 清少納言『枕草子』（國文大觀本）「ころは」（平安時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 祝ひ here means warmly blessing and celebrating loved ones on New Year's morning, matching the gift-card sense of heartfelt celebration.
context_check: positive — radiant New Year's Day passage in The Pillow Book where the sky is softly misted in spring light and everyone dresses with special care to bless and celebrate both their lord/loved ones and themselves (君をも我が身をも祝ひなどしたるさま殊にをかし)
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 祝う/祝い and ZH 祝福/慶祝 are wholly auspicious and celebratory)
notes: Theme: Light & warmth / Celebration (Phase 2 Japanese classical expansion). 祝ひ appears directly in kanji in Makura no Soshi.

meaning_in_line: to polish jade and stone to a fine, luminous finish
person_quality: patient, devoted craftsmanship and mutual refinement that brings out the best in oneself and others
line_original: 子貢曰：「《詩》云：『如切如磋，如琢如磨。』其斯之謂與？」
source: 『論語』學而第一（引『詩經』衛風・淇奧）（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 磨 here means patiently polishing jade and character through mutual refinement, matching the gift-card sense of devoted self-cultivation.
context_check: positive — Zigong and Confucius celebrating joyous self-cultivation and mutual learning
standalone_reading_risk: JP: 磨く (to polish/refine a skill or heart — wholly positive); ZH: 琢磨/切磋琢磨 (positive) vs. 折磨/磨難 ('torment/hardship' in negative compounds). Anchoring in 『論語』「如琢如磨」(切磋琢磨) keeps it entirely positive
notes: Theme: Guidance & growth. Origin of the beloved four-character idiom 切磋琢磨 used across Japan and China for friends, teammates, and mentors.

meaning_in_line: to till the fields with one's own hands in contented dedication
person_quality: patient, grounded dedication that tends the soil day by day and takes quiet joy in honest work
line_original: 開春理常業，歲功聊可觀。晨出肆微勤，日入負耒還。…但願常如此，躬耕非所歎。
source: 陶淵明「庚戌歲九月中於西田獲早稻」東晉
sense_check: Confirms match: 躬耕 here means tending the fields with one's own hands in contented dedication, matching the gift-card sense of patient, honest effort.
context_check: positive — warm autumn harvest poem celebrating setting out at dawn to do honest work, returning at sunset with the plow, and wishing 'may life always be like this — tilling with my own hands is never a cause for sighing' (但願常如此，躬耕非所歎)
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 耕す/晴耕雨読 and ZH 耕耘/深耕 evoke honest, patient cultivation of land, mind, and culture)
notes: Theme: Guidance & growth (Revised in v2: replaced Mencius's farm-taxation policy line with Tao Yuanming's warm harvest poem celebrating personal dedication and joy in one's craft).

meaning_in_line: to guide a traveler's ship safely across the vast sea
person_quality: steadfast, protective guidance that leads others safely across uncharted waters and home again
line_original: 海原の 辺にも沖にも 神づまり 領きいます 諸々の 大御神たち 船の舳に 導きまをし 天地の 大御神たち 倭の 大国御魂 久かたの 天のみ空ゆ 天翔り 見渡したまひ
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第五・894 山上憶良「好去好来の歌」（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 導き here means guiding a traveler's ship safely across the sea and home again, matching the gift-card sense of protective leadership.
context_check: positive — Yamanoue no Okura's grand blessing song ('好去好来の歌', Song of Safe Departure and Safe Return) praying for the deities of sea and sky to guide the ship's prow (船の舳に導きまをし) and bring the traveler safely home
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 導く and ZH 引導/教導 are noble, respectful verbs of mentorship and guidance; also attested in 『万葉集』巻五 沈痾自哀文「故に知る、引導は二ありと雖も、悟を得たるは惟一なりと」)
notes: Theme: Guidance & growth (Revised in v2: replaced Mencius's「導其妻子」policy line with Yamanoue no Okura's warm blessing poem「好去好来の歌」where 導きまをし appears in kanji).

meaning_in_line: to open a student's mind at the exact moment of earnest inquiry
person_quality: inspiring mentorship that waits for curiosity to ripen and then opens the door to understanding
line_original: 子曰：「不憤不啟；不悱不發。舉一隅不以三隅反，則不復也。」
source: 『論語』述而第七（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 啟 (啓) here means opening a learner's mind when curiosity ripens, matching the gift-card sense of inspiring mentorship.
context_check: positive — Confucius's famous philosophy of heuristic teaching (origin of 啓発 / 啟發): opening the way once the learner is eager to understand
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 啓く/啓発 and ZH 啟發/啟迪 are noble, intellectual, and uplifting)
notes: Theme: Guidance & growth. Shinjitai/variant 啓 corresponds to 啟 in the Analects source text (and appears as 啓 in 『枕草子』「御前に參りてありつるやうけいすれば／啓すれば」and 『万葉集』巻五「宜啓す」).

meaning_in_line: to rouse, whet, and invigorate one's spirit
person_quality: encouraging energy and disciplined dedication that inspires both oneself and others to do their best
line_original: 夫學須靜也，才須學也，非學無以廣才，非志無以成學。慆慢則不能勵精，險躁則不能冶性。
source: 諸葛亮「誡子書」三國・蜀漢
sense_check: Confirms match: 勵 here means rousing and invigorating one's spirit through calm dedication, matching the gift-card sense of encouraging energy.
context_check: positive — Zhuge Liang's tender yet earnest letter of life guidance to his young son on serenity, learning, and rousing one's spirit (勵精)
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 励む/励ます and ZH 勉勵/鼓勵/勵精圖治 are warm, encouraging, and constructive)
notes: Theme: Guidance & growth. Kyujitai 勵 / Shinjitai 励. In Japanese, 励 carries both 'working hard oneself' (励む) and 'cheering/encouraging another' (励ます).

meaning_in_line: to bank up rich earth around the roots of a growing plant
person_quality: attentive, tailored support that strengthens another person's natural talents from the roots up
line_original: 故天之生物，必因其材而篤焉。故栽者培之。
source: 『禮記』中庸・第十七章（先秦・秦漢）
sense_check: Confirms match: 培 here means banking nourishing earth around a plant's roots according to its nature, matching the gift-card sense of tailored nurturing.
context_check: positive — explaining how Heaven nurtures living things according to their innate qualities (因材施教), banking up earth around what is planted upright (栽者培之)
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 培う and ZH 栽培/培養 are warm, agricultural metaphors for building strength and character over time)
notes: Theme: Guidance & growth (Revised in v2: trimmed the contrasting clause 「傾者覆之」 from line_original so the gift card quote ends cleanly at 「故栽者培之。」).

meaning_in_line: to turn the southern riverbank lush green with spring life
person_quality: vital, transformative presence that brings fresh life and color wherever they go
fits_relationships: friend / mentor / work / parent (JP only; avoid partner in ZH)
line_original: 京口瓜洲一水間，鐘山只隔數重山。春風自綠江南岸，明月何時照我還。
source: 王安石「泊船瓜洲」北宋
sense_check: Confirms match: 綠 here is used as a living verb—spring wind turning the riverbank lush green—matching the gift-card sense of revitalizing presence.
context_check: positive — famous poem gazing across the Yangtze toward home in Jiangnan, celebrating spring's revitalizing breeze and longing for home
standalone_reading_risk: JP: 緑 (みどり, fresh greenery, nature, youth — wholly positive); ZH caution: in modern Chinese slang 綠 can refer to 'wearing a green hat' (戴綠帽, infidelity) when applied to a romantic partner. Restrict to Japanese buyers or non-partner contexts
notes: Theme: Guidance & growth. Highlighted in the ICHIREI brief as the quintessential 煉字. Textual note on Wikisource: 『王臨川集』prints「春風自綠江南岸」while Hong Mai's『容齋隨筆』transmits「春風又綠江南岸」(Kyujitai 綠 / Shinjitai 緑; also in 『和漢朗詠集』紀長谷雄「庭増気色晴沙緑」).

meaning_in_line: to renew oneself freshly each and every day
person_quality: ever-curious, forward-looking spirit that greets every day as a fresh beginning
line_original: 湯之盤銘曰：「苟日新，日日新，又日新。」
source: 『禮記』大學（先秦・秦漢）
sense_check: Confirms match: 新 here means renewing oneself freshly each day, matching the gift-card sense of ever-curious, forward-looking vitality.
context_check: positive — King Tang's inscription on his washbasin, celebrating daily moral and intellectual renewal, paired with Confucius's『論語・為政』「溫故而知新，可以為師矣」
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 新しい/新た and ZH 日新/清新 are bright, hopeful, and forward-looking)
notes: Theme: Guidance & growth. In「苟日新，日日新」, 新 functions dynamically as a verb of continual self-renewal.

meaning_in_line: broadly and open-mindedly (in learning)
person_quality: expansive curiosity and breadth of knowledge that enriches every conversation
line_original: 博學之，審問之，慎思之，明辨之，篤行之。
source: 『禮記』中庸・第二十章（先秦・秦漢）
sense_check: Confirms match: 博 here means learning broadly and open-mindedly, matching the gift-card sense of expansive curiosity and wisdom.
context_check: positive — the classic five-step sequence of scholarly and personal cultivation in the Doctrine of the Mean (also Ch. 31: 「溥博淵泉，而時出之。溥博如天，淵泉如淵」)
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 博い/博学/博愛 and ZH 淵博/博愛 are prestigious and warm)
notes: Theme: Guidance & growth (Revised in v2: kept 博 as the sole representative of Zhongyong 20's「博學之…」line, gave 審 and 慎 their own independent lines, and dropped 辨).

meaning_in_line: to appreciate deeply and understand how easily a simple room brings peace of heart
person_quality: quiet discernment that knows what truly matters in life and finds deep peace in simplicity
line_original: 倚南窗以寄傲，審容膝之易安。園日涉以成趣，門雖設而常關。
source: 陶淵明「歸去來辭」東晉
sense_check: Confirms match: 審 here means deeply appreciating how a simple home brings true peace of heart, matching the gift-card sense of quiet discernment.
context_check: positive — joyful homecoming prose-poem celebrating returning to one's true self, leaning by the sunlit southern window, and realizing how easily a cozy room brings peace (審容膝之易安)
standalone_reading_risk: JP/ZH caution: in modern everyday usage, 審 often evokes 審査 (inspection), 審判 (referee/trial), or 不審 (suspicious). Anchoring in Tao Yuanming's warm「審容膝之易安」('appreciating how easily a cozy room brings peace') transforms it into poetic contentment
notes: Theme: Guidance & growth / Quiet understanding (Revised in v2: replaced shared didactic line with Tao Yuanming's warm homecoming line「倚南窗以寄傲，審容膝之易安」).

meaning_in_line: to be mindful, reverent, and true to oneself even when alone and unseen
person_quality: quiet, unshakeable integrity that stays conscientious and true even when no one is watching
line_original: 莫見乎隱，莫顯乎微，故君子慎其獨也。
source: 『禮記』中庸・第一章（先秦・秦漢）
sense_check: Confirms match: 慎 here means staying conscientious and true to oneself even when unseen, matching the gift-card sense of quiet integrity.
context_check: positive — foundational opening chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean celebrating inner integrity in the unseen moments of life (慎其獨也; also『論語・學而』「愼終追遠，民德歸厚矣」)
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 慎む/慎重 and ZH 謹慎/慎獨 convey conscientious integrity and reverence)
notes: Theme: Guidance & growth / Memorial (Revised in v2: given its own dedicated classical line in Zhongyong Ch. 1「故君子慎其獨也」).

meaning_in_line: to bloom with ever-fresh beauty in every season
person_quality: radiant, blossoming warmth that brings fresh joy every time you meet
line_original: 時ごとにいやめづらしく咲く花を折りも折らずも見らくしよしも
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第十九・4167 大伴家持（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 咲く here means blooming with ever-fresh beauty in every season, matching the gift-card sense of radiant, blossoming warmth.
context_check: positive — Otomo no Yakamochi's joyful poem praising flowers that bloom with ever-fresh wonder in every season ('whether plucked or left on the branch, how delightful they are to behold!'; original Man'yogana text in 万葉集/第十九巻 also writes 咲 in kanji: 「毎時 弥米頭良之久 咲花乎 折毛不折毛 見良久之余志母」)
standalone_reading_risk: Cross-language delight (wholly positive): in JP 咲く means 'to blossom/bloom' (also in 『枕草子』「おもしろく咲きたる櫻を長く折りて」and 『徒然草』第139段); in classical & modern ZH 咲 is the variant of 笑 ('to smile', as in 『和漢朗詠集』紀納言「暁風緩吹。不言之唇先咲」)!
notes: Theme: Guidance & growth / Light & warmth (Revised in v2: upgraded primary row to Man'yoshu 19・4167 where 咲 appears directly in kanji in both the original Man'yogana text and Kamochi Masazumi's edition, plus Makura no Soshi and Wakan Roeishu).

meaning_in_line: to burst into bloom after winter's long seclusion
person_quality: radiant, blossoming joy that brings spring warmth after a long winter
line_original: なにはづにさくやこのはなふゆごもりいまははるべとさくやこのはな
source: 『古今和歌集仮名序』王仁の歌（平安時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: さく here means bursting into bloom after winter's seclusion, matching the gift-card sense of spring-like joy (written in kana).
context_check: positive — celebrated 'father of waka' congratulatory song celebrating blossoms bursting open in spring after winter confinement
standalone_reading_risk: none
notes: Theme: Guidance & growth (Secondary reference row marked kana_only: yes, as 咲く is written さく in the Kana Preface).

meaning_in_line: to look up to another's virtue as a sunflower turns toward the sun
person_quality: inspiring nobility of character that others naturally look up to with wholehearted trust and gratitude
line_original: 耽読吟諷し、感謝歓怡す。宜主を恋ふ誠、誠に犬馬に逾ゆ。徳を仰ぐ心、心葵カクに同じ。
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第五・吉田連宜書簡（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 仰ぐ here means looking up to another person's virtue as a sunflower turns toward the sun, matching the gift-card sense of revered leadership.
context_check: positive — warm letter of gratitude by Yoshida no Muraji Yoroshi to Otomo no Tabito in Man'yoshu Vol. 5 (original kanbun in 万葉集/第五巻: 「耽讀吟諷感謝歡怡 宜戀主之誠 誠逾犬馬仰徳之心 心同葵藿」), comparing his heart looking up to Tabito's virtue (仰徳之心 / 徳を仰ぐ心) to a sunflower turning toward the sun
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 仰ぐ/敬仰 and ZH 景仰/敬仰 express looking up with respect and gratitude; also echoed in 『詩經・小雅・車轄』「高山仰止，景行行止」)
notes: Theme: Guidance & growth / Memorial (Revised in v2: upgraded primary row to Man'yoshu Vol. 5 where 仰 appears directly in kanji in both the original kanbun and Kamochi Masazumi's edition).

meaning_in_line: to look up to with reverence as one gazes at the moon in the vast sky
person_quality: timeless grace and wisdom that others look up to like the moon in the night sky
line_original: うたのさまを（も）しり、ことのこゝろをえたらむ人は、おほぞらの月をみるがごとくに、いにしへをあふぎていまをこひざらめかも。
source: 紀貫之『古今和歌集仮名序』（平安時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: あふぎて here means looking up to timeless wisdom as one gazes at the moon, matching the gift-card sense of admiration (written in kana).
context_check: positive — grand closing passage of the Kokinshu Kana Preface, comparing reverence for the classical masters to gazing up at the moon in the vast sky
standalone_reading_risk: none
notes: Theme: Guidance & growth / Memorial (Secondary reference row marked kana_only: yes, as 仰ぎて is written あふぎて in the Kana Preface).

meaning_in_line: to flourish and prosper together with heaven and earth
person_quality: generous, life-affirming energy that helps families, teams, and communities flourish together
line_original: 天地と相栄えむと大宮を仕へまつれば貴く嬉しき
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第十九・4273 大納言巨勢朝臣（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 相栄えむ here means flourishing and prospering together in harmony, matching the gift-card sense of shared thriving.
context_check: positive — auspicious celebratory banquet poem rejoicing in serving together so that all may flourish alongside heaven and earth (天地と相栄えむと…貴く嬉しき); also in 陶淵明「歸去來辭」『木欣欣以向榮，泉涓涓而始流』
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 栄える/繁栄 and ZH 欣欣向榮/光榮 are bright, celebratory, and ideal for 還暦, retirements, and new ventures)
notes: Theme: Guidance & growth / Celebration (Phase 2 Japanese classical expansion). 相栄えむ appears directly in kanji in Kamochi Masazumi's Man'yoshu edition.

meaning_in_line: to warmly thank, comfort, and bless someone for their devoted service (労ぎたまふ / ねぎたまふ)
person_quality: warm-hearted appreciation that notices another's hard work, comforts their weariness, and celebrates their devotion
line_original: 天皇朕が 珍の御手もち 掻き撫でそ 労ぎたまふ 打ち撫でそ 労ぎたまふ 還り来む日 相飲まむ酒そ この豊御酒は
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第六・973 天皇の節度使の卿等に酒賜へる御歌（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 労ぎたまふ (ねぎたまふ) here means warmly thanking, comforting, and blessing someone for their devoted effort, matching the gift-card sense of ねぎらう.
context_check: positive — Emperor Shomu's celebratory banquet poem bestowing sacred sake (豊御酒) upon his envoys, gently stroking and thanking them (掻き撫でそ労ぎたまふ) and promising to drink together again upon their safe return.
standalone_reading_risk: In modern JP compounds, 労働/疲労 mean 'labor/fatigue', but as a verb 労う (ねぎらう) and 労わる (いたわる) mean 'to thank for hard work / care for tenderly'; in modern ZH 勞 means 'labor/toil' (though 慰勞 means 'to thank/comfort for effort'). Pair with furigana ねぎらう on the card.
notes: Live-test priority character. Replaces Tsurezuregusa 129 (where 勞 meant toil imposed on others). In Man'yoshu 6・973, 労ぎたまふ (ねぎたまふ, root of ねぎらう) is written directly with 労 in the exact gift-card sense of warmly appreciating and comforting someone's devoted effort; compare also 『周易』大象・井卦「君子以勞民勸相」.

meaning_in_line: living proof and authentic testimony of the heart (no verified kanji line)
person_quality: living proof of love and sincerity — someone whose life and steadfast actions are the truest testimony of their heart
fits_relationships: parent / partner / mentor / friend / work / memorial

context_check: none — pre-modern kanji occurrences of 證 are technical Buddhist terms (內證) or forensic witness terms (證人); kept with empty line_original per the no-weak-line rule.
