notes: no verified line — classical kanji occurrences of 證 are technical Buddhist (徒然草 157段 內證) or legal/forensic terms (徒然草 73段 證人, 論語 其父攘羊而子證之), whereas warm poetic 'living proof' in Man'yoshu is written 験 (しるし). Recommend substituting 験, 信, or 誠 when a classical quote card is required.

meaning_in_line: to shelter and protect all people under a vast, unshakeable roof
person_quality: generous, protective shelter that shields loved ones and colleagues from the wind and rain so they can smile in peace
line_original: 安得廣廈千萬間，大庇天下寒士俱歡顏，風雨不動安如山！
source: 杜甫「茅屋為秋風所破歌」唐
sense_check: Confirms match: 庇 here means sheltering and protecting people from wind and rain so all may smile in peace, matching the gift-card sense of protective shelter.
context_check: positive — although the poem begins with autumn wind tearing the poet's own thatched roof, it rises to one of the noblest humanitarian vows in world literature: wishing for a vast mansion to shelter (大庇) all people in joy, unmoved as a mountain in wind and rain
standalone_reading_risk: JP: 庇う (かばう, 'to protect/stand up for someone') and 庇 (ひさし, 'protective eaves'); minor caution in compound 庇護 (can sound slightly paternalistic if given to a peer, though warm for parents/mentors); ZH: 庇護/大庇 (protective shelter, positive)
notes: Theme: Care & nurture (Live-test engine priority character). Du Fu's 「大庇天下寒士俱歡顏，風雨不動安如山」is the supreme classical 詩眼 for 庇 (かばう).

meaning_in_line: to grant blessing, welcome, and open the clouds so all may relax as if at home
person_quality: warm, unconditional acceptance that parts the clouds and lets others untie their cords and feel completely at home
line_original: 男神も 許したまひ 女神も ちはひたまひて 時となく 雲居雨降る 筑波嶺を さやに照らして いふかりし 国のまほらを つばらかに 示したまへば 嬉しみと 紐の緒解きて 家のごと 解けてそ遊ぶ
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第九・1753 高橋虫麻呂歌集「検税使大伴の卿の筑波山に登りたまへる時の歌」（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 許したまひ here means granting warm acceptance and blessing so everyone can relax as if at home, matching the gift-card sense of generous acceptance.
context_check: positive — joyous choka celebrating Lord Otomo's ascent of Mount Tsukuba: the male deity grants his welcoming blessing (許したまひ) and the female deity bestows her grace, parting the rain clouds to shine clearly upon the fair land so the climbers loosen their cords in joy and relax as if in their own home (家のごと 解けてそ遊ぶ)
standalone_reading_risk: JP: 許す (to accept, forgive, and allow someone to be themselves, as in 心を許す 'to open one's heart in complete trust'); ZH: 嘉許/期許/應許 (praise, high hopes, promise — positive). Framing around 『心を許す』and this joyful Tsukuba poem avoids any focus on 'committing a fault that needs pardon'
notes: Theme: Quiet understanding & Acceptance (Live-test engine priority character). Also attested in 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』11・2770「道の辺の五柴原のいつもいつも人の許さむ言をし待たむ」and 『枕草子』「うへの女房のこなた許されたるなど參りて」.

meaning_in_line: to remember fondly the wishes of youth beneath the starlit bamboo
person_quality: warm, faithful remembrance that treasures shared hopes and memories across the years
line_original: 憶得少年長乞巧。竹竿頭上願糸多。
source: 『和漢朗詠集』巻上・秋・七夕 白居易（唐・平安撰）
sense_check: Confirms match: 憶 here means fondly remembering shared wishes beneath the starlit bamboo, matching the gift-card sense of faithful remembrance.
context_check: positive — nostalgic, affectionate Tanabata couplet in Wakan Roeishu ('憶ひ得たり少年の長く乞巧することを、竹竿の頭上に願糸多し') fondly recalling the many wish-threads tied to bamboo poles in youth; also paired with Bai Juyi's 「以我今朝意，憶君此夜心」and Wang Wei's 「九月九日憶山東兄弟」
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 憶える/追憶/記憶 and ZH 回憶/記憶 carry warm, poetic depth of cherished memory)
notes: Theme: Memorial & Cherished bonds (Live-test engine priority character; Japanese classical anthology row in Wakan Roeishu).

meaning_in_line: to remember and hold another's heart across the night
person_quality: deep, faithful remembrance that holds a cherished person's heart close across time and distance
line_original: 桐花詩八韻，思緒一何深。以我今朝意，憶君此夜心。
source: 白居易「初與元九別後忽夢見之及寤而書適至兼寄桐花詩悵然感懷因以此寄」唐
sense_check: Confirms match: 憶 here means holding a dear friend's heart in loving remembrance across night and distance, matching the gift-card sense of deep remembrance.
context_check: positive — Bai Juyi dreaming of his lifelong friend Yuan Zhen and waking just as Yuan's letter and paulownia-blossom poem arrive, marveling at how their hearts commune across distance ('With my heart this morning, I hold/remember your heart on that night')
standalone_reading_risk: none
notes: Theme: Memorial & Cherished bonds (Chinese Tang poetry companion row for 憶).

meaning_in_line: to make a solemn, enduring vow of the heart (no verified kanji line)
person_quality: steadfast devotion that keeps a sacred promise alive across every season and year

meaning_in_line: wholehearted faith and trust that brings unforeseen blessings
person_quality: unwavering trustworthiness and wholehearted faith that anchors every relationship
line_original: 深く信をいたしぬれば、かゝる德もありけるにこそ。
source: 吉田兼好『徒然草』（國文大觀本）第六十八段（鎌倉・南北朝時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 信 here means wholehearted faith and trustworthiness that brings lasting virtue, matching the gift-card sense of unwavering trust.

standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 信じる/信頼/信義 and ZH 誠信/信賴/信念 are among the highest human virtues in both languages)

meaning_in_line: generous grace and kindness bestowed warmly upon a humble recipient
person_quality: life-shaping kindness and generosity that the giver will never forget

source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第五・藤原房前書簡（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 恩 here means generous, life-sustaining kindness bestowed upon the recipient, matching the gift-card sense of unforgettable grace.
context_check: positive — Fujiwara no Fusasaki's gracious letter in Man'yoshu Vol. 5 thanking Otomo no Tabito for his gift of a paulownia koto (original kanbun in 万葉集/第五巻: 「跪承芳音 嘉懽交深 乃知 龍門之恩復厚蓬身之上」), rejoicing in deep gratitude that his benefactor's kindness lies thick and warm upon him; also in 『徒然草』第142段「恩愛の道ならでは、かゝるものゝ心に慈悲ありなむや。孝養の心なきものも、子もちてこそ親の志はおもひ知るなれ。」
standalone_reading_risk: JP/ZH directionality note: 恩 (恩恵/恩師/報恩/恩愛) is deeply moving when given **from a child, student, or junior to a parent, mentor, or benefactor** (expressing gratitude for received grace), or between spouses as 恩愛, but should NEVER be given from a superior to a subordinate (where it would sound like 'demanding gratitude' / 恩着せがましい)
notes: Theme: Care & nurture / Gratitude (Live-test engine priority character). Appears directly in kanji in Man'yoshu Vol. 5 and Tsurezuregusa 142段; engine rule should restrict 恩 to upward/gratitude or partner/memorial gifts.

meaning_in_line: to add warmth and joy to every season by conversing unhurriedly and sharing a cup with a friend (興を添ふる)
person_quality: gentle, unobtrusive accompaniment (寄り添う・添える) that quietly enriches another person's life simply by being beside them
fits_relationships: partner / parent / friend / mentor / child / work
line_original: 月の夜、雪の朝、花のもとにても、心のどかに物語して、杯いだしたる、萬の興を添ふるわざなり。つれ〴〵なる日、思ひの外に友の入り來て、取り行ひたるも心慰む。
source: 吉田兼好『徒然草 (校註日本文學大系)』第百七十五段（鎌倉・南北朝時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 添ふる here means adding joy and warmth to life by conversing unhurriedly and sharing a cup with a companion, matching the gift-card sense of 寄り添う・添える.
context_check: positive — at the close of Section 175, Kenko celebrates the warm, human moments when sharing a quiet conversation and a cup beneath the moon, snow, or blossoms—or welcoming an unexpected friend—adds joy to all things (萬の興を添ふるわざなり).
standalone_reading_risk: none in JP (添う/寄り添う/添える are among the warmest, most idiomatic Japanese verbs for standing by someone's side and adding a thoughtful touch); ZH: 增添/添福 (to add/increase blessings, positive)
notes: Upgraded from landscape verse (煙添柳色看猶浅) to a warm, person-centered passage in Tsurezuregusa 175 where 添ふる directly describes companionship enriching life across moonlit nights, snowy mornings, and spring blossoms.

meaning_in_line: to support and sustain another person (no verified kanji line)
person_quality: steadfast, quiet support that sustains another person through every climb and season
sense_check: No verified kanji line; classical kanji occurrences refer to branches or props while warm Japanese uses of 支える are in kana, so line_original is left empty per the no-weak-line rule.
context_check: none — classical kanji occurrences of 支 mean tree branches, limbs (四支), or propping up a collapsing building, while warm Japanese uses of 支える are written in kana; kept with empty line_original per the no-weak-line rule.
standalone_reading_risk: JP: 支える (ささえる, 'to support/sustain' — one of the most beloved everyday Japanese gift words); ZH caution: in modern Chinese standalone 支 often functions as a measure word or 'branch' (分支/支配), though 支持/支柱 ('support/pillar') are positive. For classical purists, 扶 or 輔 or 載 (厚德載物) are stronger classical verbs of 'supporting', while 支 is included for Japanese 支える stories
notes: no verified line — previous quote (從來支許遊) used 支許 as the proper names Zhi Dun (支遁) and Xu Xun (許詢). In classical texts 支える is written in kana (e.g., おくのほそ道『鳥海天をさゝへ』) or refers to physical props. Recommend substituting 扶 (row 8), 輔, or 添 (row 94) when a classical quote card is required.

meaning_in_line: to glow in harmonious radiance with crimson robes
person_quality: warm, luminous presence and grace that brightens the whole room
line_original: しげいしやの繪に書きたるやうに美くしげにて居させ給へるに、宮いとやすらかに今すこしおとなびさせ給へる御けしきの紅の御ぞに匂ひ合せ給ひて、なほたぐひはいかでかと見えさせ給ふ。
source: 清少納言『枕草子』（國文大觀本）「淑景舎、東宮にまゐり給ふほどのことなど」（平安時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 匂ひ合せ給ひて here means glowing in harmonious visual radiance and grace, matching the gift-card sense of luminous presence.
context_check: positive — glowing court scene in The Pillow Book admiring Empress Teishi's serene, matured grace radiating in harmony with her crimson robes (紅の御ぞに匂ひ合せ給ひて), truly beyond compare; also in 『徒然草』第44段「夜さむの風にさそはれくる、そらだき物の匂も身にしむこゝちす」
standalone_reading_risk: Caution: in classical JP にほふ meant 'to glow with radiant color/aura' and 'sweet fragrance', whereas in modern JP 匂う/臭う can mean generic 'smell/odor' (and 匂わせ is slang for social-media hinting); in ZH 匂 is a Japanese kokuji not used in standard Chinese. Prefer 薫 or 馨 for general gift carving
notes: Theme: Memorial & constancy (Revised in v2: upgraded primary row to Makura no Soshi where 匂ひ合せ給ひて is written directly in kanji in its original sense of radiant visual harmony, while keeping Kokinshu 42 as secondary kana_only: yes row).

meaning_in_line: to bloom with the exact same fragrance and living warmth as in years past
person_quality: unchanging warmth and grace that lingers in the heart and never fades with time

standalone_reading_risk: See primary 匂 row (prefer 薫 or 馨 for standalone carving)
notes: Theme: Memorial & constancy (Secondary reference row marked kana_only: yes, as 匂ひける is written にほひける in the Kokinshu text).

meaning_in_line: to breathe forth noble fragrance like orchids perfuming a garment's sash
person_quality: quiet, noble grace whose influence lingers warmly in the air long after a meeting
line_original: 于時初春令月 氣淑風和梅披鏡前之粉 蘭薫珮後之香
source: 『万葉集』巻五・815 梅花歌卅二首并序（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 薫 here means breathing forth noble fragrance that lingers warmly on one's robes, matching the gift-card sense of refined, lasting influence.
context_check: positive — the joyous Dazaifu plum-blossom banquet preface (source of the Reiwa era name), celebrating early spring, gentle breezes, and orchids perfuming sashes (also in 『和漢朗詠集』村上天皇「漸薫臘雪新封裏」and 後中書王「花薫紫麝凱風程」)
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 薫る/薫陶 and ZH 薰陶/溫馨 carry exclusively refined, noble associations of sweet scent and moral mentorship)
notes: Theme: Memorial / Guidance & growth. Far safer than 匂 in modern standalone reading, carrying both 'fragrant memory' and 'mentorship' (薫陶).

meaning_in_line: precious, revered, and deeply cherished upon beholding
person_quality: irreplaceable dignity and worth that commands love and reverence simply by existing
line_original: 父母を 見れば貴し 妻子見れば めぐし愛し 世間は かくぞことわり
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第五・800 山上憶良（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 貴し here means beholding one's parents with deep reverence and love, matching the gift-card sense of irreplaceable dignity and worth.
context_check: positive — Yamanoue no Okura's warm affirmation of human family bonds: looking upon one's parents, they are revered and precious (父母を見れば貴し); looking upon one's spouse and children, they are dear and lovely; also written logographically as 貴 in 『万葉集』巻十九・4255 大伴家持「秋時花 種尓有等 色別尓 見之明良牟流 今日之貴左」(今日の貴さ)
standalone_reading_risk: none (both JP 貴い/尊い and ZH 珍貴/高貴 are universally noble and reverent)
notes: Theme: Care & nurture / Memorial (Revised in v2: cited Kamochi Masazumi's Man'yoshu edition where 貴し appears directly in kanji, corroborated by Yakamochi's logographic 今日之貴左 in Man'yoshu 19・4255).

meaning_in_line: to surpass all worldly treasures in worth (no verified kanji line)
person_quality: surpassing worth and inner excellence that outshines silver, gold, and jewels

standalone_reading_risk: JP/ZH caution: standalone 勝 usually evokes 'winning/defeating an opponent' (勝負/勝利/勝敗) rather than 'excelling in grace/surpassing in worth' (勝れる / まさる). Use only when the giver specifically wants the 'excellence/victory' nuance or pairs it with the classical text

person_quality: being the greatest treasure in the giver's life, surpassing all worldly wealth
line_original: 銀母 金母玉母 奈尓世武尓 麻佐礼留多可良 古尓斯迦米夜母

meaning_in_line: to bring supreme solace and comfort to the heart
person_quality: gentle, healing presence that comforts the heart like conversing with a cherished friend beneath a warm lamp
line_original: ひとり燈のもとに文をひろげて、見ぬ人を友とするこそこよなう慰むわざなれ。
source: 吉田兼好『徒然草』（國文大觀本）第十三段（鎌倉・南北朝時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 慰む here means bringing supreme solace and comfort to the heart through quiet companionship, matching the gift-card sense of gentle comfort.
context_check: positive — beloved passage in Tsurezuregusa 13段 on the supreme solace (こよなう慰むわざなれ) of opening a book beneath a lamp and befriending wise souls; also in 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』9・1757「草枕 旅の 憂けくを 慰むる こともあれやと」and 『枕草子』「思ひ歎かれつる心も慰みて嬉しきに」

meaning_in_line: quietly and contemplatively (treasuring knowledge in the heart)
person_quality: quiet, unboastful absorption of wisdom paired with tireless learning and teaching (DO NOT USE as standalone gift — benchmark row)
fits_relationships: work / mentor (DO NOT USE as standalone gift — benchmark row)

meaning_in_line: to welcome the arrival of spring and its life-giving rain and dew

person_quality: sunny, open-hearted brightness (朗らか) that clears away gloom like the moon in an open sky

person_quality: auspicious, celebratory warmth (ことほぐ) that blesses loved ones with long life and enduring vitality

meaning_in_line: to pile up ever more richly and abundantly like new-year snow (いや重け吉事)
person_quality: steady, cumulative richness of character that layers kindness upon kindness and brings compounding good fortune
line_original: 新しき年の初めの初春の今日降る雪のいや重け吉事
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第二十・4516 大伴家持（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: いや重け here means good things layering and accumulating ever more richly, matching the gift-card sense of treasuring accumulated years and kindness (重ねる・重んじる).
context_check: positive — the celebrated final poem (4516) closing the entire twenty-volume Man'yoshu, praying that auspicious blessings pile up like the snow on New Year's Day.
standalone_reading_risk: In modern JP, 重い alone can mean 'heavy/burdensome', whereas 重ねる (to layer time/care) and 重んじる (to value) are deeply positive; specify reading かさねる/おもんじる on the card.
notes: Phase 2 addition (Steadfast Constancy & Blessing).

meaning_in_line: to fill heaven and earth with radiant sufficiency and contentment (足らはし照りて)
person_quality: deep, grounded contentment (足るを知る・心足らふ) that brings fullness of heart to everyone around them
line_original: 天地に足らはし照りて我が大王敷きませばかも楽しき小里
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第十九・4272 大伴家持（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 足らはし here means filling the world with radiant fullness and satisfaction, matching the gift-card sense of inner sufficiency and contentment (満ち足りる).
context_check: positive — auspicious banquet poem praising how radiant, all-filling grace makes even the local village a place of joy.
standalone_reading_risk: Standalone 足 is commonly read あし ('foot/leg') in modern JP and ZH; when used for 'sufficiency/contentment' (たる / たらう), include furigana たる on the gift card.
notes: Phase 2 addition. Also in 18・4094『老人も女童児もしが願ふ心足らひに撫で賜ひ治め賜へば』.

meaning_in_line: enduring and long-lasting alongside heaven and earth across ten thousand ages (天地と長く久しく)
person_quality: timeless, enduring constancy that stays true across decades without ever fading
line_original: 天地と 長く久しく 万代に 変らずあらむ 行幸の宮
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第三・315 大伴旅人（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 久しく here means enduring unchanged for ten thousand ages alongside heaven and earth, matching the gift-card sense of lasting constancy and longevity.
context_check: positive — Otomo no Tabito's celebratory poem at Yoshino Palace blessing it to endure unchanged forever alongside heaven and earth.
standalone_reading_risk: none (久しい / 悠久 / 永久 is auspicious in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Steadfast Constancy & Memorial).

meaning_in_line: in peaceful safety, calm health, and unruffled well-being (平らけく)
person_quality: peaceful, grounding equanimity (平らか) that keeps the household calm and safe through every journey
line_original: あり巡り我が来るまでに平らけく親はいまさね恙無く妻は待たせと住吉の我が皇神に幣奉り祈り申して
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第二十・4408 大伴家持（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 平らけく here means living in peaceful safety and calm health until a loved one returns, matching the gift-card sense of serene peace and well-being.
context_check: positive — heartfelt prayer to the deity of Sumiyoshi asking that one's parents remain in peaceful health (平らけく親はいまさね) and one's spouse wait safely without harm.
standalone_reading_risk: In modern JP/ZH, 平 alone can sometimes be read as 'ordinary/flat' (平凡), so frame with the classical reading たいらか (peaceful, serene, safe as in 泰平/平安).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Care & Peace). Also in 5・897『現の限りは平らけく安くもあらむを』.

meaning_in_line: pure, crystal-clear, and refreshing to the soul (川の瀬の浄きを見れば)
person_quality: unsullied, crystal-clear integrity of heart that refreshes everyone who encounters it
line_original: あしひきの み山も清に 落ち激つ 芳野の川の 川の瀬の 浄きを見れば 上辺には 千鳥数鳴き 下辺には かはづ妻呼ぶ
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第六・920 笠金村（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 浄き (きよき) here means crystal-clear purity that inspires a prayer for everlasting life, matching the gift-card sense of pure-hearted integrity.
context_check: positive — Kasa no Kanamura praises the pure rapids of Yoshino and concludes by praying to the gods of heaven and earth that the court flourish forever (万代にかくしもがもと天地の神をぞ祈る).
standalone_reading_risk: In JP Buddhist usage 清浄/浄土 has spiritual overtones (making it especially fitting for memorials as well as elders with spiritual depth).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Quiet Understanding & Memorial).

meaning_in_line: to bring people and things into harmonious, cared-for order (撫で賜ひ整へ賜ひ)
person_quality: calm, attentive orderliness that brings harmony, care, and readiness to any home or team
line_original: もののふの 八十伴男を 撫で賜ひ 整へ賜ひ 食す国の 四方の人をも あぶさはず 恵み賜へば
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第十九・4254 大伴家持（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 整へ賜ひ here is paired with 撫で賜ひ to mean bringing everyone into harmonious order through loving care, matching the gift-card sense of thoughtful coordination.
context_check: positive — celebratory poem praising benevolent leadership that cares for and harmonizes all people without leaving anyone behind.
standalone_reading_risk: none (整える / 整う is positive and respected in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Steadfast Constancy & Work). Also in Tsurezuregusa 220『物の音のめでたく整ほり侍ること、外よりも勝れたり』.

meaning_in_line: to revere and hold in the highest esteem an honest, unpretentious nobility of character (尤尊ぶべし)
person_quality: quiet, unpretentious nobility of spirit that commands deep respect without ever seeking display
fits_relationships: parent / mentor / partner / friend / work / memorial
line_original: 剛毅木訥の仁に近きたぐひ氣稟の淸質尤尊ぶべし
source: 松尾芭蕉『おくのほそ道』仏五左衛門・日光（江戸時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 尊ぶべし here means deeply revering an honest, pure-hearted person whose quiet integrity approaches true benevolence, matching the gift-card sense of reverence.
context_check: positive — Basho warmly praises his host Hotoke Gozaemon for his honest, completely unpretentious kindness, comparing him to Confucius's ideal of 'firm, resolute, simple, and unassuming' (剛毅木訥) and declaring such pure nature most worthy of reverence.
standalone_reading_risk: none (尊い / 尊ぶ / 尊敬 is universally positive and reverent in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Quiet Understanding & Reverence). Also appears in Tsurezuregusa 39『いと尊かりけり』.

meaning_in_line: peaceful, tranquil, and secure in daily life beneath benevolent light (國民安堵の栖穩かなり)
person_quality: serene, reassuring presence (穏やか) that makes home and daily life feel safe, calm, and peaceful
line_original: 今此御光一天にかゞやきて恩澤八荒にあふれ國民安堵の栖穩かなり
source: 松尾芭蕉『おくのほそ道』日光（江戸時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 穩かなり (穏やかなり) here means a peaceful, tranquil, and secure home life blessed by overflowing kindness, matching the gift-card sense of calm warmth.
context_check: positive — Basho celebrates the radiant peace and overflowing grace at Nikko in glorious May sunshine, where people's homes rest in tranquil security.
standalone_reading_risk: none (穏やか / 安穏 is warm and positive in both JP and ZH; note kyujitai 穩 in the Edo-period text).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Steadfast Constancy & Peace). Uses kyujitai 穩 in the original orthography.

meaning_in_line: to illuminate radiantly like the morning sun shining on vermilion walls (朝日朱の玉垣を輝かす)
person_quality: morning-sun radiance that brightens everyone around them and brings out the brilliance in their surroundings
fits_relationships: partner / child / friend / mentor / parent / work
line_original: 宮ばしらふとしく彩椽きらびやかに石の階九仭にかさなり朝日朱の玉垣を輝かす
source: 松尾芭蕉『おくのほそ道』塩竈（江戸時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 輝かす here means the morning sun illuminating the sacred shrine in brilliant light, matching the gift-card sense of radiant, uplifting brilliance.
context_check: positive — Basho's awe-filled morning visit to Shiogama Shrine, marveling at the morning sun illuminating the vermilion fence and celebrating the deep spiritual heritage of the land.
standalone_reading_risk: none (輝く / 輝き is universally bright and positive in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Light & Warmth).

meaning_in_line: to rejoice wholeheartedly in sharing a journey and caring for a companion's hardships (ともにせん事を悅び)
person_quality: warm, companionable joy that delights in walking alongside others and sharing both beauty and hardship
line_original: このたび松島象潟の眺めともにせん事を悅びかつは羈旅の難をいたはらんと旅立曉髪を剃て墨染にさまをかえ惣五を改て宗悟とす
source: 松尾芭蕉『おくのほそ道』黒羽・曾良（江戸時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 悅び (悦び) here means rejoicing in sharing life's journey with a friend while tenderly looking after their hardships, matching the gift-card sense of heartfelt joy.
context_check: positive — Basho's deeply affectionate portrait of his traveling companion Sora, who rejoiced to share the sights of Matsushima and Kisagata and devotedly cared for Basho on the road.
standalone_reading_risk: none (悦び / 喜悦 is refined and positive in both JP and ZH; note kyujitai 悅 in original text).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Light & Warmth / Companionship). Also in『論語』學而第一「學而時習之，不亦說（悅）乎」.

meaning_in_line: deeply gentle, refined, and full of tender human feeling (優に情ありける)
person_quality: tender, empathetic gentleness (優しい・優美) that honors human feelings without judgment
fits_relationships: parent / partner / friend / mentor / child / memorial
line_original: 法顯三藏の天竺に渡りて、故郷の扇を見ては悲しび、病に臥しては漢の食を願ひ給ひける事を聞きて、「さばかりの人の、無下にこそ、心弱き氣色を、人の國にて見え給ひけれ。」と人のいひしに、弘融僧都、「優に情ありける三藏かな。」といひたりしこそ、法師の樣にもあらず、心にくく覺えしか。
source: 吉田兼好『徒然草 (校註日本文學大系)』第八十四段（鎌倉・南北朝時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 優に情ありける here combines refined grace and warm human tenderness, matching both modern Japanese senses of 優 (優しい 'kind/tender' and 優れる 'admirable').
context_check: positive — Kenko warmly admires the monk Koyu for defending Faxian's homesickness in India with the empathetic words, 'What a gentle, warm-hearted master he was!' (優に情ありける三藏かな). For shorter card printing, use『弘融僧都、「優に情ありける三藏かな」といひたりしこそ…心にくく覺えしか』.
standalone_reading_risk: none (優しい and 優れる are among the most beloved positive words in Japanese; in ZH 優雅/優秀 means 'graceful/excellent').
notes: Phase 2 addition (Care & Nurture / Quiet Understanding).

meaning_in_line: to look back upon and cherish the noble character of a revered teacher with fond longing (彼見佛聖の寺はいづくにやと慕はる)
person_quality: warm, magnetic virtue that others naturally look up to, cherish, and hold dear in their hearts
line_original: 雲居禪師の德化によりて七堂いから改りて金壁壯嚴光かゝやき佛土成就の大伽藍とはなれりける彼見佛聖の寺はいづくにやと慕はる
source: 松尾芭蕉『おくのほそ道』瑞巌寺（江戸時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 慕はる here means fondly admiring and longing after a person of pure virtue, matching the gift-card sense of loving admiration and remembrance (慕う).
context_check: positive — at gleaming Zuiganji Temple, Basho marvels at Ungo Zenji's transformative virtue and fondly longs after the ancient sage Kenbutsu Hijiri.
standalone_reading_risk: none (慕う / 敬慕 / 思慕 is warm, respectful, and ideal for mentors, parents, and memorials in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Memorial & Mentor). Also in Tsurezuregusa 22『何事も古き世のみぞ慕はしき』.

meaning_in_line: a true friend of generous heart, healing care, and wisdom (善き友三つあり)
person_quality: true, life-enriching companionship that gives generously, heals, and shares wisdom
line_original: 善き友三つあり。一にはものくるゝ友、二には醫師、三には智惠ある友。
source: 吉田兼好『徒然草 (校註日本文學大系)』第百十七段（鎌倉・南北朝時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 善き友 here defines the qualities of a true friend—generosity, healing care, and wisdom—matching the gift-card sense of cherished friendship.
context_check: positive — Kenko's famous distillation of the three kinds of good friends who enrich, heal, and guide our lives (also paired with Section 13『ひとり燈火のもとに文をひろげて、見ぬ世の人を友とするこそ、こよなう慰むわざなれ』).
standalone_reading_risk: none (友 / 友情 / 親友 is universally warm in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Companionship).

meaning_in_line: to nurture life and help others in fulfilment of loyalty and filial devotion (身を養ひ人を助け)
person_quality: practical, compassionate help that sustains others and fulfills love through concrete action
line_original: 次に醫術を習ふべし。身を養ひ人を助け、忠孝のつとめも、醫にあらずばあるべからず。
source: 吉田兼好『徒然草 (校註日本文學大系)』第百二十二段（鎌倉・南北朝時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 人を助け here directly means helping and sustaining other people through practical skill and care, matching the gift-card sense of reliable help.
context_check: positive — Kenko outlines the essential arts a person should cultivate, placing the art of healing and helping others (身を養ひ人を助け) at the heart of loyalty and filial care.
standalone_reading_risk: none (助ける / 助け合い is universally positive in both JP and ZH; excellent verified-quote alternative to 支).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Care & Support — verified classical alternative to 支).

meaning_in_line: to be conscientious, humble, and unpretentiously mindful in all one's conduct (愚かにして謹めるは得の本なり)
person_quality: humble, conscientious mindfulness that never cuts corners and forms the true root of excellence
line_original: 萬の道の人、たとひ不堪なりといへども、堪能の非家の人にならぶ時、必ずまさることは、たゆみなく愼みて輕々しくせぬと、偏に自由なるとの等しからぬなり。藝能所作のみにあらず、大方の振舞、心づかひも、愚かにして謹めるは得の本なり、巧みにしてほしきまゝなるは失の本なり。
source: 吉田兼好『徒然草 (校註日本文學大系)』第百八十七段（鎌倉・南北朝時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 謹める here means humble, unflagging conscientiousness in craft and daily conduct, matching the gift-card sense of sincere diligence.
context_check: positive — Kenko explains why a dedicated practitioner always surpasses a flashy amateur: unflagging mindfulness and humble conscientiousness (たゆみなく愼みて…謹めるは得の本なり) are the true foundation of mastery.
standalone_reading_risk: Avoid 謹慎 (disciplinary confinement); in gift context frame as 謹む (conscientious, reverent, sincere).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Strength & Work). Also provides a Japanese classical companion line for 慎 (たゆみなく愼みて).

meaning_in_line: wise and noble in heart, continually growing from wisdom to greater wisdom (心はなどか、賢きより賢きにも、うつさば移らざらむ)
person_quality: ever-deepening wisdom of heart that grows through reflection and humility rather than outward show
line_original: 人品容貌こそ生れつきたらめ、心はなどか、賢きより賢きにも、うつさば移らざらむ。
source: 吉田兼好『徒然草 (校註日本文學大系)』第一段（鎌倉・南北朝時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 賢き here specifically praises the inner wisdom of the heart (心) growing ever wiser through effort, matching the gift-card sense of inner wisdom.
context_check: positive — directly contrasts fixed outward appearance with the boundless capacity of the human heart to grow from wisdom to greater wisdom (賢きより賢きにも). Also echoed in『論語』里仁第四「見賢思齊焉」.
standalone_reading_risk: none (賢い / 賢明 / 賢人 is universally positive in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Guidance & Growth).

meaning_in_line: at peace and unburdened in heart (身を閑にし、事に與らずして心を安くせむこそ)
person_quality: serene, reassuring peace of heart (安らか・安心) that puts everyone around them at ease
line_original: いまだ誠の道を知らずとも、縁を離れて身を閑にし、事に與らずして心を安くせむこそ、暫く樂しぶともいひつべけれ。
source: 吉田兼好『徒然草 (校註日本文學大系)』第七十五段（鎌倉・南北朝時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 心を安くせむ here means bringing calm, unburdened peace to the heart, matching the gift-card sense of 安らぎ / 安らか.
context_check: positive — Kenko reflects on how stepping back from worldly noise to keep the heart peaceful (心を安くせむ) brings true joy; also supported by Man'yoshu 5・897『現の限りは平らけく安くもあらむを』and Tao Yuanming『審容膝之易安』.
standalone_reading_risk: In modern JP, 安い alone can mean 'inexpensive/cheap'; on the gift card, specify the classical and literary reading やすらか (peaceful, serene, reassuring, as in 安らぎ/安心/平安).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Quiet Understanding & Peace).

meaning_in_line: to pledge evergreen constancy with the pine and cypress that never wither in frost (契松柏之後凋)
person_quality: unbreakable promise and kindred bond (契り) that stays evergreen through every frost and season
line_original: 嵐陰欲暮。契松柏之後凋。
source: 『和漢朗詠集』巻上・秋・菊 紀長谷雄（平安時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 契 here means pledging a solemn, enduring bond of constancy like the evergreen pine and cypress, matching the gift-card sense of a sacred promise (契り).
context_check: positive — Ki no Haseo praises the chrysanthemum's noble resilience, pledging brotherhood with the evergreen pine and cypress (alluding to Confucius's『歲寒，然後知松柏之後凋也』).
standalone_reading_risk: In modern ZH/JP, 契約 means 'legal contract', whereas in Japanese literary usage 契り / 契る means a deep, sacred bond or vow between people; ideal verified-quote substitute for 誓.
notes: Phase 2 addition (Steadfast Constancy — verified classical substitute for 誓).

meaning_in_line: to treasure and hold dear every moment of spring and youth shared with a companion (踏花同惜少年春)
person_quality: tender, appreciative heart (惜しむ・愛惜) that never takes a single shared moment or person for granted
line_original: 背燭共憐深夜月。踏花同惜少年春。
source: 『和漢朗詠集』巻上・春・春夜 白居易「春中与盧四周諒華陽観同居」（唐・平安撰）
sense_check: Confirms match: 同惜 here means cherishing and treasuring precious time together with a dear friend beneath the blossoms, matching the gift-card sense of treasuring someone deeply.
context_check: positive — Bai Juyi recalls staying with his close friend Lu Liang at Huayang Monastery in spring, turning away from the candle to admire the midnight moon together and treading blossoms while cherishing their springtime youth.
standalone_reading_risk: In modern JP/ZH, 惜しい / 可惜 can mean 'regrettable/a pity', while 惜しむ / 珍惜 means 'to treasure, value, and hold dear'; frame with the sense of 慈しみ惜しむ / 珍惜 on the card.
notes: Phase 2 addition (Care & Memorial). Also in Tsurezuregusa 108『寸陰を惜む人なし…唯今の一念空しくすぐることを惜むべし』.

meaning_in_line: to warmly invite, encourage, and host companions like the spring breeze (樽前勧酔是春風)
person_quality: warm, encouraging hospitality that lifts others' spirits as naturally as the spring breeze
line_original: 花下忘帰因美景。樽前勧酔是春風。
source: 『和漢朗詠集』巻上・春・春興 白居易「菩提寺上方晩眺」（唐・平安撰）
sense_check: Confirms match: 勧 here means warmly inviting and encouraging companions to enjoy the moment like the spring breeze, matching the gift-card sense of warm encouragement (勧める).
context_check: positive — one of the most beloved couplets in Wakan Roeishu, celebrating a joyful spring gathering where the beauty of the blossoms makes guests forget to go home and the spring breeze itself plays host.
standalone_reading_risk: none (勧める / 勧学 is positive and encouraging in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Light & Warmth / Guidance). Also in『荀子』勸學 and『周易』井卦「君子以勞民勸相」.

meaning_in_line: to polish and make gems sparkle in the sunlight and breeze (瑩日瑩風)
person_quality: luminous, gem-like clarity that polishes every work and shines brightly in the sun and wind
line_original: 瑩日瑩風。高低千顆万顆之玉。染枝染浪。表裏一入再入之紅。
source: 『和漢朗詠集』巻上・春・花 菅原文時（平安時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 瑩 (みがく・かがやく) here is used as a vivid verb meaning to polish and shine like thousands of jewels in the sun and breeze, matching the gift-card sense of luminous refinement.
context_check: positive — Sugawara no Fumitoki's celebrated couplet in Wakan Roeishu praising spring blossoms gleaming like thousands of polished jewels in the sun and wind.
standalone_reading_risk: none (晶瑩 / 瑩然 is a refined literary character for gem-like luster and clarity in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Light & Warmth / Craftsmanship). Classic example of 煉字 (adjective/noun used as an active verb: 日に瑩き風に瑩く).

meaning_in_line: to pass down and hear across generations the memory of compassionate wisdom (ほのかに傳へ聞くに)
person_quality: faithful transmission of wisdom, kindness, and cultural memory from one generation to the next
line_original: ほのかに傳へ聞くに、いにしへのかしこき御代には、あはれみをもて國ををさめ給ふ。…これ民をめぐみ、世をたすけ給ふによりてなり。
source: 鴨長明『方丈記』（國文大觀本・鎌倉時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 傳へ聞く (伝へ聞く) here means handing down across time the story of compassionate care that blesses and helps the world, matching the gift-card sense of passing on wisdom and kindness.
context_check: positive — a warm passage in Hojoki recalling the compassionate rule of ancient sage-emperors who governed with mercy to bless the people and help the world (民をめぐみ、世をたすけ給ふ).
standalone_reading_risk: none (伝える / 伝承 / 伝統 is universally positive in both JP and ZH; uses kyujitai 傳 in the original text).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Guidance & Memorial).

meaning_in_line: to flourish in full, vibrant prime like the capital in spring (咲く花の薫ふがごとく今盛りなり)
person_quality: vibrant, generous energy that brings every gathering and endeavor into full, fragrant bloom
line_original: あをによし寧楽の京師は咲く花の薫ふがごとく今盛りなり
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第三・328 小野老（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 今盛りなり here means flourishing in radiant, fragrant prime right now, matching the gift-card sense of vibrant thriving and celebration (especially for 還暦 and milestones).
context_check: positive — Ono no Oyu's celebrated song of praise for the Nara capital flourishing like fragrant blossoms in full bloom.

notes: Phase 2 addition (Strength & Radiance — ideal for 60th birthday / 還暦 celebrating that life is 'now in full bloom').

meaning_in_line: living proof and joyful fulfillment of being alive in a flourishing age (生ける験あり)
person_quality: living proof (生けるしるし) that makes every effort and year of life feel deeply worthwhile
fits_relationships: parent / partner / mentor / friend / work / memorial

source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第六・996 海犬養宿禰岡麻呂（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 生ける験あり (いけるしるしあり) here means feeling the joyful, tangible proof of being alive, providing the authentic classical Japanese kanji for 'living proof' (しるし).

standalone_reading_risk: In modern JP/ZH, 試験/実験 means 'exam/experiment'; on a gift card, always include furigana しるし and the Man'yoshu line『生ける験あり』.
notes: Phase 2 addition — authentic Man'yoshu kanji for 'living proof' (しるし), serving as the verified classical counterpart to 証 (row 86).

meaning_in_line: to shine and gleam like a precious gem hidden among the rocks (石隠り燿ふ玉)
person_quality: inner brilliance that gleams quietly like a gem even when not seeking the spotlight
line_original: 見渡せば近きものから石隠り燿ふ玉を取らずはやまじ
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第六・951 笠金村（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 燿ふ (かがよふ) here means gleaming with irresistible inner radiance like a jewel, matching the gift-card sense of luminous personal worth.

standalone_reading_risk: none (かがやく / かがよう is radiant and auspicious in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Light & Warmth).

meaning_in_line: to rejoice wholeheartedly upon reading a cherished friend's words (耽読吟諷し、感謝歓怡す)
person_quality: wholehearted, welcoming delight (歓び) that rejoices in another person's voice and presence
line_original: 耽読吟諷し、感謝歓怡す。宜主を恋ふ誠、誠に犬馬に逾ゆ。徳を仰ぐ心、心葵カクに同じ。
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第五・吉田連宜書簡（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 感謝歓怡す here uses 歓 to mean rejoicing with wholehearted gladness upon receiving a friend's words, matching the gift-card sense of warm joy and welcome (歓び).

standalone_reading_risk: none (歓び / 歓待 / 歓喜 is universally positive in both JP and ZH; good safe alternative to 迎 when expressing 'warm welcome').
notes: Phase 2 addition (Light & Warmth — safe 'welcome/joy' alternative to 迎).

meaning_in_line: to rejoice with serene, harmonious gladness of heart (耽読吟諷し、感謝歓怡す)
person_quality: serene, gentle cheerfulness (怡び・和らぎよろこぶ) that warms family and friends
line_original: 耽読吟諷し、感謝歓怡す。
source: 『万葉集 (鹿持雅澄訓訂)』巻第五・吉田連宜書簡（奈良時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 歓怡す here means rejoicing with serene, warm gladness of spirit, matching the gift-card sense of gentle joy.
context_check: positive — warm expression of gratitude and gladness in Man'yoshu Volume 5; also in『論語』子路第十三「兄弟怡怡」('brothers in warm, genial harmony').
standalone_reading_risk: none (怡然 / 心曠神怡 is refined and wholly positive in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Light & Warmth).

meaning_in_line: graceful, lovely, and radiant in bearing (繪に書きたるやうに美くしげにて居させ給へるに)
person_quality: inner and outer grace (美しさ) that brings harmony and dignity to every moment
line_original: しげいしやの繪に書きたるやうに美くしげにて居させ給へるに、宮いとやすらかに今すこしおとなびさせ給へる御けしきの紅の御ぞに匂ひ合せ給ひて、なほたぐひはいかでかと見えさせ給ふ。
source: 清少納言『枕草子』（國文大觀本）「淑景舎、東宮にまゐり給ふほどのことなど」（平安時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 美くしげにて here expresses affectionate, radiant loveliness and grace in a warm family setting, matching the gift-card sense of beauty of heart and bearing.
context_check: positive — Sei Shonagon's warm, admiring portrait of the two sisters (Empress Teishi and Shigeisha) sitting together in affectionate harmony; also paired with『論語』顏淵「君子成人之美」(inner moral beauty).
standalone_reading_risk: none (美しい / 美徳 is universally positive in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Light & Grace).

meaning_in_line: serenely unhurried and free from worldly clamor (縁を離れて身を閑にし)
person_quality: tranquil, unhurried poise (閑か・のどか) that creates a peaceful sanctuary away from the world's rush
line_original: いまだ誠の道を知らずとも、縁を離れて身を閑にし、事に與らずして心を安くせむこそ、暫く樂しぶともいひつべけれ。
source: 吉田兼好『徒然草 (校註日本文學大系)』第七十五段（鎌倉・南北朝時代）
sense_check: Confirms match: 身を閑にし (みをしづかにし) here means keeping one's life serenely unhurried and peaceful, matching the gift-card sense of tranquil composure (閑雅・静閑).
context_check: positive — Kenko praises the quiet joy of stepping back from worldly entanglements to live in serene peace; also in Wakan Roeishu『竹院君閑銷永日』.
standalone_reading_risk: In modern JP, 閑 alone can be read ひま ('idle/unbusy', as in 閑散), whereas in classical literature 閑 (しづか / のどか, as in 閑雅・閑静) means 'serenely tranquil and refined'. Use furigana しずか or のどか on the card.
notes: Phase 2 addition (Quiet Understanding).

meaning_in_line: to cultivate and refine one's own character with sincerity of heart (欲齊其家者，先修其身)
person_quality: quiet, lifelong self-cultivation that leads family and colleagues by personal example
line_original: 欲齊其家者，先修其身；欲修其身者，先正其心；欲正其心者，先誠其意。
source: 『禮記』大學（先秦・秦漢）
sense_check: Confirms match: 修其身 here means cultivating one's own character through sincerity and uprightness of heart, matching the gift-card sense of lifelong self-refinement (修養・修める).
context_check: positive — the foundational passage of the Great Learning linking sincere inner cultivation (誠意・正心・修身) to family harmony.
standalone_reading_risk: none (修める / 修養 is dignified and positive in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Guidance & Growth).

meaning_in_line: to set one's heart straight and true in sincerity (欲修其身者，先正其心)
person_quality: unwavering fairness and uprightness of heart that serves as a moral compass for others
line_original: 欲修其身者，先正其心；欲正其心者，先誠其意。
source: 『禮記』大學（先秦・秦漢）
sense_check: Confirms match: 正其心 here means setting one's heart upright and true through sincerity, matching the gift-card sense of honest integrity (正しい).
context_check: positive — core teaching of the Great Learning on cultivating an upright, sincere heart; also echoed in Tsurezuregusa 85『人の心すなほならねば、僞りなきにしもあらず、されど自ら正直の人などかなからむ』.
standalone_reading_risk: none (正しい / 正直 / 正義 is universally positive in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Strength & Integrity).

meaning_in_line: unadorned, pure white silk; beholding and keeping one's natural, unpretentious self (見素抱樸)
person_quality: unadorned, natural honesty (素直・素朴) that shines without pretense or artifice
line_original: 見素抱樸，少私寡欲。
source: 『老子』道德經・第十九章（唐玄宗御註本・先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 素 here means pure, undyed silk representing natural, unpretentious genuineness of heart, matching the gift-card sense of 素直 / ありのまま.
context_check: positive — Laozi's celebrated call to return to pure, unadorned simplicity and uncarved authenticity; also appears in Tsurezuregusa 194『素直に眞と思ひて』.
standalone_reading_risk: none (素直 / 素敵 / 素朴 is warm and beloved in modern JP; in ZH 純素/樸素 means 'pure and simple').
notes: Phase 2 addition (Quiet Understanding & Authenticity).

meaning_in_line: pure-hearted, kind, and genuinely good in disposition (夫子溫、良、恭、儉、讓以得之)
person_quality: innate, unforced goodness and kindness of heart (善良・良さ) that everyone immediately trusts
fits_relationships: parent / partner / friend / mentor / child / work
line_original: 夫子溫、良、恭、儉、讓以得之。夫子之求之也，其諸異乎人之求之與！
source: 『論語』學而第一（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 良 here describes Confucius's pure, kind-hearted goodness alongside warmth (溫) and courtesy (恭), matching the gift-card sense of genuine goodness.
context_check: positive — Zigong's affectionate portrait of how Confucius won people's hearts not by demand, but through warmth, goodness, respectfulness, restraint, and deference.
standalone_reading_risk: none (良い / 善良 / 良心 is universally positive in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Care & Goodness).

meaning_in_line: courteous, reverent, and considerate in every interaction with others (與人恭而有禮)
person_quality: warm, attentive courtesy (うやうやしい・礼儀正しい) that treats every person with dignity and makes them feel like family
line_original: 君子敬而無失，與人恭而有禮，四海之內，皆兄弟也。
source: 『論語』顏淵第十二（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 與人恭而有禮 here means treating others with sincere, respectful courtesy that turns all people within the four seas into brothers, matching the gift-card sense of respectful warmth.
context_check: positive — Zixia consoles Sima Niu by reminding him that a person who is reverent without fault and courteous toward others has brothers everywhere within the four seas.
standalone_reading_risk: none (恭しい / 恭敬 / 恭賀 is dignified and auspicious in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Quiet Understanding & Respect).

meaning_in_line: humble, deferential, and generously yielding credit and place to others (溫、良、恭、儉、讓)
person_quality: unselfish modesty (譲る・謙譲) that quietly steps back to let others shine
line_original: 夫子溫、良、恭、儉、讓以得之。夫子之求之也，其諸異乎人之求之與！
source: 『論語』學而第一（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 讓 (譲) here means generous deference and humility that puts others first, matching the gift-card sense of unselfish grace (譲り合い).
context_check: positive — one of the five cardinal personal virtues of Confucius praised by Zigong.
standalone_reading_risk: none (譲る / 謙譲 / 礼譲 is admired as a core virtue in both JP and ZH; uses traditional 讓 in the Chinese text).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Quiet Understanding & Humility).

meaning_in_line: to support, assist, and strengthen one another's benevolence through friendship (以友輔仁)
person_quality: steadfast, uplifting support (輔ける) that walks beside a friend or partner and brings out their best

source: 『論語』顏淵第十二（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 輔 here means supporting and strengthening a friend's benevolence and character, matching the gift-card sense of mutual support (たすける・支え合う).
context_check: positive — Zengzi's famous closing aphorism of Analects Book 12 on how noble friends gather through learning and support each other in benevolence.
standalone_reading_risk: none (相輔相成 / 輔佐 is dignified and positive in both JP and ZH; prime verified-quote substitute for 支).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Care & Support — prime classical substitute for 支).

meaning_in_line: to help others fulfill and bring to fruition their finest qualities (君子成人之美)
person_quality: generous mentorship and encouragement that helps others achieve their dreams and bring out their best
line_original: 子曰：「君子成人之美，不成人之惡。小人反是。」
source: 『論語』顏淵第十二（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 成人之美 here uses 成 as a transitive verb to help others fulfill their finest qualities, matching the gift-card sense of nurturing accomplishment.

standalone_reading_risk: none (成す / 成長 / 大成 is universally positive in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Guidance & Growth).

meaning_in_line: humble modesty—holding a mountain's height quietly within the earth—that gives fairly to all (地中有山，謙)
person_quality: deep, mountain-within-the-earth humility that carries great capability without a trace of pride
line_original: 謙：地中有山，謙；君子以裒多益寡，稱物平施。
source: 『周易』大象・謙卦（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 謙 here is imaged as a lofty mountain hidden quietly inside the level earth, matching the gift-card sense of true humility paired with inner stature.
context_check: positive — Hexagram 15 (謙) is the only hexagram in the entire I Ching where all six lines are auspicious (六爻皆吉), celebrating humility that balances and benefits everyone.
standalone_reading_risk: none (謙虚 / 謙遜 is one of the most admired virtues in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Quiet Understanding & Humility).

meaning_in_line: gentle, steady cultivation of virtue that grows from small beginnings to great height like a tree rising from the earth (君子以順德，積小以高大)
person_quality: gentle, unforced steadiness that accumulates small daily acts of kindness into something tall and enduring
line_original: 升：地中生木，升；君子以順德，積小以高大。
source: 『周易』大象・升卦（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 順德 here means cultivating virtue with gentle, natural steadiness like a tree growing from the earth, matching the gift-card sense of harmonious, steady growth.
context_check: positive — the Great Image of Hexagram 46 (Sheng, Ascending), comparing a noble person's steady accumulation of virtue to a tree growing tall from within the earth.
standalone_reading_risk: In modern JP, 従順 can sound overly submissive if used alone; frame via this I Ching line as natural, steady harmony and auspicious flow (順調 / 順風 / 順徳).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Guidance & Growth).

meaning_in_line: to shine forth and illuminate radiant virtue like the sun rising above the earth (君子以自昭明德)
person_quality: sunrise clarity and open-hearted integrity that illuminates the path for others
line_original: 晉：明出地上，晉；君子以自昭明德。
source: 『周易』大象・晉卦（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 昭 here is used as a verb meaning to make one's bright virtue shine forth like the sun rising over the earth, matching the gift-card sense of luminous integrity.
context_check: positive — the Great Image of Hexagram 35 (Jin, Progress/Sunrise); also echoed in『詩經』小雅・鹿鳴「我有嘉賓，德音孔昭」.
standalone_reading_risk: none (in JP 昭 is also loved by the Showa generation, making this classical pre-Qin source especially meaningful for elders).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Light & Warmth).

meaning_in_line: to practice, learn, and discuss together with friends like two lakes nourishing each other (君子以朋友講習)
person_quality: lifelong joy in learning and practicing alongside friends, mutually enriching one another
line_original: 兌：麗澤，兌；君子以朋友講習。
source: 『周易』大象・兌卦（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 講習 here means learning and practicing in joyful fellowship, matching the gift-card sense of humble, lifelong learning (習う・学び続ける).
context_check: positive — the Great Image of Hexagram 58 (Dui, Joyousness), imaging two joined lakes that replenish each other just as friends learn and practice together; also in『論語』學而「學而時習之，不亦說乎」.
standalone_reading_risk: none (習う / 学習 is positive and humble in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Guidance & Growth).

meaning_in_line: to feel warm closeness and affection toward one's teacher and companions (安其學而親其師)
person_quality: warm, approachable kindness (親しみ・親切) that makes students, colleagues, and family feel immediately close and cared for
line_original: 安其學而親其師，樂其友而信其道，是以雖離師輔而不反也。

sense_check: Confirms match: 親其師 here uses 親 as a verb meaning to feel warm affection and closeness toward a mentor, matching the gift-card sense of approachable warmth (親しみ・親切) as well as parental love (親).
context_check: positive — the Record of Learning explains how warm mentorship inspires students to love their learning, draw close to their teacher, rejoice in their friends, and stay true to the way for life.
standalone_reading_risk: none (works beautifully both as おや 'parent' and したしむ/しんせつ 'warm closeness/kindness' in JP and 親切/親愛 in ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Care & Mentorship).

meaning_in_line: to nurture and help another person's good qualities grow (教也者，長善而救其失者也)
person_quality: patient mentorship that spots what is good in another person and helps it grow tall
line_original: 知其心，然後能救其失也。教也者，長善而救其失者也。
source: 『禮記』學記（先秦・秦漢）
sense_check: Confirms match: 長善 here uses 長 (ちょうずる・のばす) as a verb meaning to foster and grow another person's strengths after understanding their heart, matching the gift-card sense of nurturing leadership.
context_check: positive — one of the finest definitions of teaching and leadership in classical literature: first understanding a person's heart (知其心) and then nurturing their strengths (長善).
standalone_reading_risk: none (成長 / 長所を伸ばす / 長寿 is positive across both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Guidance & Growth).

meaning_in_line: to respond to a simple gift with precious jade—not merely to repay, but to seal an everlasting friendship (報之以瓊瑤，匪報也，永以為好也)
person_quality: wholehearted gratitude (報いる・恩返し) that answers every kindness with tenfold warmth and lasting affection
line_original: 投我以木桃，報之以瓊瑤，匪報也，永以為好也。
source: 『詩經』衛風・木瓜（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 報 here means responding to another's kindness with generous gratitude to build an everlasting bond, matching the gift-card sense of heartfelt reciprocity (報いる).
context_check: positive — the classic Book of Odes poem of gratitude and enduring friendship, celebrating giving back not as a transaction (匪報也) but to cherish each other forever (永以為好也).
standalone_reading_risk: In modern JP/ZH, 報 can appear in 報復 ('retaliation') or 報道 ('news report'), so pair explicitly with this Shijing line to anchor the warm sense of 恩に報いる.
notes: Phase 2 addition (Gratitude & Reciprocity).

meaning_in_line: enduring affection, harmony, and cherished friendship forever (永以為好也)
person_quality: warm, enduring affection (好意・よしみ) that treasures a bond for a lifetime
line_original: 投我以木瓜，報之以瓊琚，匪報也，永以為好也。
source: 『詩經』衛風・木瓜（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 好 here means deep, lasting affection and amity between people (永以為好也), matching the gift-card sense of loving fondness.
context_check: positive — joyful celebration of mutual giving and lifelong friendship in the Book of Odes.
standalone_reading_risk: none (好ましい / 好意 / 友好 is warm and positive in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Care & Affection).

meaning_in_line: to treasure and hold someone dear in the very center of one's heart, never forgetting them for a single day (中心藏之，何日忘之)
person_quality: deep, quiet devotion that holds a cherished person in the center of the heart through every day and year
line_original: 心乎愛矣，遐不謂矣？中心藏之，何日忘之？
source: 『詩經』小雅・隰桑（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 中心藏之 here means treasuring a loved one deep within one's heart and never forgetting them for a single day, matching the gift-card sense of abiding remembrance and deep love.
context_check: positive — the speaker admires a noble person beneath the lush mulberry trees and declares that because they love them in their heart, they treasure them in their innermost core and could never forget them for a single day.

notes: Phase 2 addition (Memorial & Deep Love — one of the most moving memorial and partner lines in all of classical literature).

meaning_in_line: to bring warm harmony, peace, and blessing to one's home and family (宜其室家)
person_quality: warm, harmonizing presence that makes a home and family flourish in peace and affection
line_original: 桃之夭夭，灼灼其華，之子于歸，宜其室家。
source: 『詩經』周南・桃夭（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 宜其室家 here uses 宜 (よろしくす・むつまじくす) as a verb meaning to bring harmony and warmth to a home, matching the gift-card sense of harmonious family warmth.
context_check: positive — the quintessential wedding and household blessing song of the Book of Odes, comparing a bride to radiant peach blossoms and blessing the harmony she brings to her home.
standalone_reading_risk: none (むべ・よろし in JP and 相宜/合宜 in ZH are auspicious and refined).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Care & Family Harmony). Also echoed in『禮記』中庸「宜爾室家，樂爾妻帑」.

meaning_in_line: deep, brimming, and lasting in harmonious joy (和樂且湛)
person_quality: deep, quiet fullness of spirit (湛える) that holds joy, wisdom, and warmth like deep clear water
line_original: 我有嘉賓，鼓瑟鼓琴。鼓瑟鼓琴，和樂且湛。
source: 『詩經』小雅・鹿鳴（先秦）
sense_check: Confirms match: 和樂且湛 here means harmonious joy that is deep, brimming, and enduring, matching the gift-card sense of a smile or heart brimming with quiet depth (たたえる).
context_check: positive — from the celebrated hospitality ode Lu Ming (quoted also in the Doctrine of the Mean), welcoming honored guests with zithers and lutes in deep, harmonious joy.
standalone_reading_risk: none (湛える 'to brim with a smile/water' in JP and 精湛/湛藍 in ZH are literary and positive).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Light & Warmth / Quiet Depth).

meaning_in_line: unshakeably firm and resilient through a thousand trials and winds from every direction (千磨萬擊還堅勁)
person_quality: unshakeable, bamboo-like resilience and reliability that stands firm through every storm
line_original: 咬定青山不放鬆，立根原在破巖中。千磨萬擊還堅勁，任爾東西南北風。
source: 鄭燮「竹石」清
sense_check: Confirms match: 堅勁 here means standing firm and unyielding through a thousand trials, matching the gift-card sense of steadfast reliability and grit (堅実・堅固).
context_check: positive — Zheng Xie (Zheng Banqiao)'s celebrated inscription on bamboo rooted in mountain rock, standing ever firmer and more resilient no matter which way the winds blow.

notes: Phase 2 addition (Strength & Endurance).

meaning_in_line: deeper than a thousand-foot peach-blossom pool in friendship and affection (桃花潭水深千尺，不及汪倫送我情)
person_quality: deep, bottomless warmth of heart and thoughtfulness whose affection outmeasures any words
line_original: 桃花潭水深千尺，不及汪倫送我情。
source: 李白「贈汪倫」唐
sense_check: Confirms match: 深 here measures the depth of human affection and friendship—even a thousand-foot pool is not as deep as Wang Lun's heart—matching the gift-card sense of deep heart and thought.
context_check: positive — Li Bai's joyful, affectionate thank-you poem to his host Wang Lun, who came singing to see him off by Peach Blossom Pool; also echoed in Man'yoshu 5・藤原房前書簡『嘉懽交深し』.
standalone_reading_risk: none (深い / 情が深い / 深みがある is universally positive in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Quiet Understanding & Friendship).

meaning_in_line: to share the same luminous moon together across a thousand miles (但願人長久，千里共嬋娟)
person_quality: wholehearted togetherness (共にする・分かち合う) that shares life's joys and stays connected across any distance
line_original: 但願人長久，千里共嬋娟。
source: 蘇軾「水調歌頭（明月幾時有）」北宋
sense_check: Confirms match: 共 here means sharing the beauty of the moon together in heart even across a thousand miles, matching the gift-card sense of walking and sharing life together (共に歩む).
context_check: positive — although composed when Su Shi missed his brother Su Zhe at Mid-Autumn, the poem resolves into one of the most famous affirmative blessings in East Asian literature: wishing loved ones long life (但願人長久) and sharing the luminous moon across any distance.
standalone_reading_risk: none (共に / 共感 / 共鳴 is warm and positive in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Companionship & Memorial).

meaning_in_line: to share the same clouds, rain, and bright moon as one heart across two places (青山一道同雲雨，明月何曾是兩鄉)
person_quality: kindred-spirit solidarity (同じ心) that shares the same sky and stands united no matter the distance
line_original: 青山一道同雲雨，明月何曾是兩鄉。
source: 王昌齡「送柴侍御」唐
sense_check: Confirms match: 同雲雨 here uses 同 as a verb meaning to share the same clouds and rain along a single mountain range, matching the gift-card sense of kindred unity (心を同じくする).
context_check: positive — Wang Changling reassures his friend Chai Shiyu that because the green mountains connect them under the same clouds, rain, and bright moon, they are never truly in two separate lands; also echoed in Tsurezuregusa 12『同じ心ならむ人と、しめやかに物語して』.
standalone_reading_risk: none (同志 / 同心 is warm and unifying in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Companionship).

meaning_in_line: to recognize, appreciate, and honor a person's true worth (天下誰人不識君)
person_quality: discerning insight and appreciative recognition (見識・知己) that sees a person's true talent and worth
line_original: 莫愁前路無知己，天下誰人不識君。
source: 高適「別董大二首（其一）」唐
sense_check: Confirms match: 識君 here means recognizing and honoring a friend's true worth and character, matching the gift-card sense of deep discernment and appreciation.
context_check: positive — Gao Shi's rousing, optimistic encouragement to his musician friend Dong Tinglan, assuring him that the whole world recognizes his worth.
standalone_reading_risk: none (見識 / 識者 / 良識 is respected and positive in both JP and ZH).
notes: Phase 2 addition (Guidance & Recognition).
